title: Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive
description:
Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive brings together album covers, book jackets, magazines, film stills, photographs, prints, and other ephemera featuring the work of Charles White (1918-1979) to examine the expansive cultural life of his imagery. Tracing how his work circulated beyond the studio and the museum wall, the exhibition reveals how White’s images centered everyday life and shaped a broader visual language.
 An artist who worked fluidly across drawing, painting, printmaking, and mural-making, White created what he described as “powerful images of dignity”, centering African-American experiences as well as historical figures and events at a time when such representations were widely distorted or excluded from mainstream culture. These opportunities for reproduction arose through active collaboration with musicians, writers, and filmmakers. White’s images were adapted, printed, and distributed across a wide range of media, crossing disciplines and communities to become part of a shared cultural consciousness.
 By foregrounding circulation alongside creation, the exhibition invites visitors to consider how White’s work contributed to the formation of a Black visual canon. His images did not remain fixed objects behind glass — they became living symbols, connecting people, histories, and communities through a sustained commitment to representation, relationships, and what White himself understood as a sense of oneness.
 Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive is a special initiative of the Charles White Archives presented by Logan Center Exhibitions and the South Side Community Art Center. The exhibition is curated by Ian White with curatorial support by Paulina Alvarez, Jan Brugger, and jada-amina. Additional support is provided by the Ng Family Visiting Artist Fund, the Revada Foundation, and Friends of the Logan Center.

title: Pierre Bismuth: Love Bless America
location: Neubauer Collegium for Culture and Society
description:
This exhibition features new works by the French artist and filmmaker Pierre Bismuth. The centerpiece is a long-form meditative film documenting a creative collaboration between Joshua Abrams and Sharon Udoh, two leading figures from Chicago’s jazz and improvised music scene. Bismuth tasked them with composing a 21st-century spiritual based on a lyrical hymn he wrote for the project. The film traces the magic and workaday practice of “inspiration,” taking the traditions of religious music as a point of departure for a multi-layered reflection on love, music, and the divine. In addition to this new film, Bismuth will present a series of digital images resembling American flags emblazoned with lyrics from the hymn.
 Curated by Dieter Roelstraete.
 The Neubauer Collegium Gallery is free and open to the public. Gallery hours: M–F, 9–4.
 The Neubauer Collegium Gallery is supported by the Neubauer Family Foundation and the Brenda Mulmed Shapiro Fund. Additional support for this exhibition was provided by Bernard Friedman, the Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, and the France Chicago Center at the University of Chicago.

title: Anne Frank The Exhibition
location: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
address: 5700 S Lake Shore Drive, Chicago, IL, 60637
description:
ANNE FRANK: THE EXHIBITIONat Griffin MSI
Anne Frank The Exhibition is an immersive, full-scale recreation of the Annex where Anne Frank, her family and four other Jewish inhabitants lived in hiding during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Griffin Museum of Science and Industry is the first museum in the Midwest to present this exhibition, and Chicago is only the second U.S. city to host this extraordinary experience, featuring never-before-seen artifacts from Anne Frank’s life. 
Explore the world that shaped Anne’s story, from her early childhood in Frankfurt through the rise of Nazi Germany and the spread of antisemitism across Europe, to the Frank family’s move to Amsterdam. There, Anne lived for nearly ten years, including the final two, which were spent in hiding. 
Step inside the meticulously reconstructed Annex and reflect on the daily challenges, risks and courage of those who hid there before their arrest and deportation in 1944.
Anne Frank The Exhibition is a presentation of the Anne Frank House.

title: Autumn Carillon Tower Tours
description:
Carillon Tower Tours are at 11:30 AM and 4:30 PM Tuesdays - Fridays.
 The Laura Spelman Rockefeller Memorial Carillon and its sister instrument at Riverside Church in New York City, both dating from the early 1930s, were the masterworks of the Gillett & Johnston bell foundry of Croydon, England. Carillons of this size had never before been made, and have not been made again since that time. The Chicago instrument, comprising 72 bells and 100 tons of bronze, is the single largest musical instrument ever built. Its bells were cast over a three-year period and include a massive 18.5 ton bourdon sounding a low C#.
 In 271 steps we can show you the bells from the perspective of our carillon students and peregrine falcons! The spiral stone staircase is taken at a leisurely pace, and is not recommended for those who are claustrophobic. Along the way you’ll walk above the Chapel’s false ceiling (the attic, via a catwalk), through the mechanical room housing the original carillon regulator clock as well as the pneumatically-driven mechanism of the quarter and hour chimes, past the largest bell (36,926 lbs at 117 inches in diameter) and its 13 friends, and then into the playing cabin, 240 of the 271 steps up, where the carillonneur plays the mighty instrument. Beyond the cabin, another short winding staircase leads the way to the top of the tower. In season and when permitted by the University, magnificent 360-degree views of Chicago, Lake Michigan, northern Indiana, the Michigan Harbor Country shoreline, and the University itself are available.
 Please note that the tour is not suitable for children under the age of 5. Young children and anyone unable to ascend the stone steps may watch the recital free of charge in the Chapel itself from one of two viewing stations in the west transept and narthex. Check in at the front desk to set off for the 45-minute round-trip climb. Carillon tours are capped at 15 guests.
 The carillon is played live in recital each weekday of the academic year at 12 PM and 5 PM, and on Sunday mornings after the 11 AM service. Members of the University of Chicago Guild of Carillonists are happy to incorporate requests into the daily recitals.

title: “I Don’t Care If They Call Me a Dictator”: Atrocities in the Bukele Model
description:
The lecture will examine the human rights consequences of the security model implemented by President Nayib Bukele in El Salvador, particularly since the declaration of the state of exception in March 2022. It will analyze patterns of mass arbitrary detention, torture and ill-treatment, enforced disappearance, deaths in custody, persecution, and sexual and gender-based violence, as well as the concentration of political power and the dismantling of judicial safeguards and institutional checks on executive authority. Drawing on the findings of the International Group of Independent Experts on El Salvador (GIPES), the presentation will also assess whether these patterns may amount to crimes against humanity under international law and reflect on the broader implications of the “Bukele model” as an increasingly influential approach to security policy in Latin America.
 José Antonio Guevara Bermúdez is a Mexican lawyer, human rights expert, and academic with more than 25 years of experience in international human rights law, international criminal law, transitional justice, and international humanitarian law. He is currently Academic Director of the Memory and Tolerance Museum in Mexico City and Associate Professor at the Autonomous University of Tlaxcala.
 From 2014 to 2020, he served as a member and Chair-Rapporteur of the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention, and as a member of the Coordination Committee of the UN Human Rights Council’s Special Procedures. He previously served as Executive Director of the Mexican Commission for the Defense and Promotion of Human Rights and held senior human rights positions in the Mexican government and diplomatic service, including at Mexico’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations in Geneva.
 He has taught at universities in Mexico and abroad and was Tinker Visiting Professor at the University of Chicago in 2025. He is the author and co-author of numerous publications on human rights and international justice. He holds a Law Degree from Universidad Iberoamericana and a Ph.D. in Fundamental Rights from Universidad Carlos III de Madrid.
 This event is organized by the Center for Latin American and Caribbean Studies (CLACS) with support from the Pozen Family Center for Human Rights.

title: Setting Fire to Reason: A Framework for Free Speech and Its Limits
description:

 Using incitement as his central example, Howard sets out a framework of speakers’ rights and duties, determining when and why speech restrictions can be justified. title: Intentionality, 1960: Whose Dreams? Gallery Hours
description:
Arts + Public Life at the University of Chicago presents Intentionality, 1960: Whose Dreams? a new exhibition by Chicago artist Candace Hunter centered on the construction of the Dan Ryan Expressway and the Black communities displaced in its path. Now embedded within Chicago’s physical and social fabric, the Dan Ryan Expressway obscures both the choices that produced it and the lives reorganized around it. The construction disrupted the ordinary intimacies through which a place becomes home: routes traveled, neighbors known, businesses frequented, porches gathered on.
 Through photographic collage, architectural fragments, archival materials, sound, sculptural interventions, and oral histories, Hunter moves between what is documented and what is remembered. The work resists the idea that displacement can be understood solely through statistics.
 The series builds on the Memory Teas Candace hosted during her APL residency, which gathered first-person accounts from Black Chicagoans who remember the Dan Ryan’s construction and the neighborhoods transformed by it. Rather than asking these memories to complete the historical record, Hunter allows them to stay partial, layered, and unresolved.
 While centered on Chicago’s South Side, the history at the heart of Intentionality, 1960 reaches beyond the city. Across the United States, highway construction, redevelopment, and urban renewal reshaped Black communities, often presenting profound social and spatial disruption as necessary progress. Intentionality, 1960 invites audiences to see those histories not as isolated events but as part of a larger American story.
 Intentionality, 1960 will be accompanied by Threshold: Conversations on the Stoop, a series of public dialogues on the front porch within the exhibition between Candace and scholars to dive into topics related to the exhibition. The Threshold conversations are presented with support from the Office of the Provost Diversity and Inclusion team, in partnership with the Chicago Forum for Free Inquiry and Expression.
 Intentionality, 1960: Whose Dreams? will be on view from September 24-December 12 in the Arts + Public Life Gallery Space located in the Arts Incubator at 301 E. Garfield Blvd.
 Gallery Hours: Thursday-Saturday | 1:00 - 5:00pm

title: Richard III: Monstrous Villain or Slandered King
description:
At the beginning of Shakespeare’s play Richard III, Richard, alone on stage states that “I am determinèd to prove a villain.” And so he does—murdering any who stand in his way with abandon. But was the historical Richard really such a villain? During his brother Edward IV’s reign Richard was known for his loyalty and competence. But on his brother’s death in 1483, Richard declared his nephews illegitimate and took the crown. The uncrowned twelve year old Edward V and his younger brother Richard were lodged in the Tower, and not seen again. In 1485 Henry Tudor, Earl of Richmond, defeated Richard at the Battle of Bosworth field, where Richard was killed. The new king Henry VII had his followers present Richard as a monster who among those he murdered were the Princes in the Tower. Thus, Henry’s victory saved England. In this class we examine the successes and failures of Richard’s life and reign, how the view of the villainous Richard developed, and then in more recent centuries, was countered by some historians as well as enthusiasts who formed the Richard III society.
Carole Levin, Willa Cather Professor of History Emerita of the University of Nebraska, is the author or editor of over twenty books as well as a playwright and poet, and has won awards for her teaching.

title: LECTURE “The King Can Do No Wrong”: Daniel Lee, Berkeley
location: Social Sciences Research Building, Tea Room (201)
description:
It is settled law that states, owing to their sovereignty, are immune from suit. This principle of sovereign immunity, however, is a relatively recent innovation in the history of modern public law. For this talk, I’d like to trace some of the origins of this principle, beginning with one of the earliest decisions from the United States Supreme Court, Chisholm v. Georgia (1793). The lone dissent by Justice Iredell in Chisholm is noteworthy, not only because it anticipated the Eleventh Amendment to the U.S. Constitution, but also because it engineered the fundamentals of sovereign immunity in a deliberately archaic manner, following the English common law principle, ‘The King can do no wrong,’ in sources such as Blackstone, Coke, and the Year Books. Some questions: How much of this principle is ultimately rooted in a secularized theological concept of impeccability? Who can ‘do no wrong’ in a republic, where there can be no kings?
 ABOUT THE AUTHOR
 Daniel Lee is Professor of Political Science at the University of California, Berkeley, and holds a courtesy faculty appointment in the UC Berkeley School of Law
 . He specializes in political theory, the history of political thought, legal history, and jurisprudence. His research concerns the legal science of Roman law in modern political thought and its continuing influence on modern doctrines of statehood, sovereignty, rights, and international law. He is an internationally renowned authority on the legal and political thought of Jean Bodin and Hugo Grotius. In his current research, he is interested in the relationship between legal science and social science in the history of ideas, as well as the foundations of deontic logic in early modern jurisprudence and social science.
 His books include Popular Sovereignty in Early Modern Constitutional Thought
 (Oxford, 2016), The Right of Sovereignty: Jean Bodin on the Sovereign State and the Law of Nations
 (Oxford, 2021), and Divisions of Law 
 (Oxford, 2026). He was also a co-editor (with Cornel Zwierlein) of Sovereignty: European and Global Histories, 1400-1800 (Brill, 2025)
 .
 He is currently working on two new projects. Sacrosanct is under contract with Harvard University Press. The Science of Right
 traces the foundations of legal science and natural law in modern jurisprudence from Grotius to Hohfeld.

title: Perrin Roosevelt Ireland on “Poking the Squid: What We Can Learn from Animal Sex”
location: Centers for Gender/Race Studies, Community Room (105)
description:
Author Perrin Roosevelt Ireland on her book Poking the Squid: What We Can Learn from Animal Sex, in conversation with UChicago’s Rachel Moran, Assistant Professor of Ecology and Evolution 
 About the book: The secret sex lives of animals are not so secret anymore, thanks to this brilliant, punchy illustrated guide to how the other 99.99% get it on. In delightful watercolor comics of pregnant seahorse dads, spider oral sex, and the four-headed echidna penis, Perrin Roosevelt Ireland takes us on a wild biodiversity ride through queerness, infidelity, consent, divorce, sex change, and even sexual cannibalism in the animal world. Poking the Squid illustrates the splendid diversity of nature’s eroticism. For too long, science has prudishly obscured the wildly creative kinkiness of animal sexual behavior. But Poking the Squid celebrates how assumptions about sex are shifting.
 About the author: Perrin Roosevelt Ireland is an artist an
d environmentalist. For a decade, she worked at the Natural Resources Defense Council (NRDC), ultimately as deputy to the executive director. Her artwork has been published in Discover, Nature, Scientific American, and The Rumpus. She serves on the board of the Roosevelt Institute, was an inaugural Artist in Residence at the New York Aquarium and is a Banff Graphic Novel Resident. Perrin lives in Brooklyn, New York, with her cats (and muses) Ursula and Pudge.
About the interlocutor: Rachel Moran is an assistant professor in the Department of Ecology & Evolution at the University of Chicago. Her research explores how reproductive behaviors evolve and contribute to the formation of new species, using freshwater fishes as a model system. Her lab combines behavioral experiments, genomics, and neural imaging approaches to study mate choice, aggression, parental care, and hybridization.
 Presented by the Center for the Study of Gender and Sexuality, the Gray Center for Arts and Inquiry, and the Biological Sciences Divison.

title: Unfixed: Identity, Expression & Creative Freedom, a Student Workshop with Jenn Freeman | Po’Chop
description:
This student workshop is part of the Dialogue in Action: Art, Citizenship, and Expression project, funded by a grant from The Chicago Forum for Free Inquiry and Expression, led by Andrei Pop and Jessica Musselwhite.
 This interactive and embodied student workshop explores the relationship between identity, creative risk, and freedom. Through movement, reflection, improvisation, and collaborative exercises, participants will consider how identity shapes and informs how we express ourselves, how we are seen by others, and what we believe is possible. Unfixed invites participants to experiment beyond fixed expectations and explore what becomes possible when we give ourselves permission to be uncertain, contradictory, expansive, and unfinished.
 Participants should wear comfortable clothing they can move in and bring materials to write with.
 Space is limited to 20 people. If you RSVP and your plans change, please let us know so we can offer your spot to someone on the wait list.
 About Jenn Freeman | Po’Chop
Jenn Freeman is an interdisciplinary artist who creates on the homeland of the Council of the Three Fires: The Odawa, Council of the Three Fires: The Odawa, Ojibwe and Potawatomi Nations; as well as the Miami, Ho-Chunk, Sauk and Meskwaki; the Kiikaapoi, Peoria, and the Očeti Šakówiŋ (Sioux) Nations. Freeman, also known as Po’Chop, weaves dance, storytelling, drag and striptease together to create experiences that illuminate Black queer life. She is a co-founder of House of the Lorde, a multi-functional space rooted in Black feminist praxis, the co-producer of the adored Notes on Masculinity, a drag king centered cabaret and creator of The Black Burlesque Directory, an archive of Black burlesque performers across the world. Freeman has collaborated with Jamila Woods, Anna Martine Whitehead and VAM Studio. Her work has been supported by Foundation of Contemporary Art, DANCE/USA, Urban Bush Women, United States Artists and Chicago Dancemakers Forum.

title:
A Homecoming in Poetry: An Evening with Dylan Lloyd 
Author of Coffee Walk Poetry
description:
The University of Chicago Library is proud to co-sponsor a reading and signing with Dylan Lloyd, author of the Amazon #1 bestselling poetry collection Coffee Walk Poetry — and a writer with deep roots in the University of Chicago community.
 Dylan Lloyd is the grandson of Monte Lloyd, the beloved Professor Emeritus of Ecology and Evolution at UChicago whose pioneering research on periodical cicadas made him one of Chicago’s most celebrated scientists. Dylan grew up with Hyde Park in his bones — his father renovated homes throughout the neighborhood, and the streets around 54th and Ellis were part of the family’s story for generations.
 Coffee Walk Poetry was born from those same streets. Written during the quietude of the COVID years, the collection grew out of Dylan’s daily walks through Hyde Park — poems composed in the time it took to walk to Starbucks and back, capturing grief, resilience, love, and the beauty hidden in ordinary moments.
 Today, Dylan has built a career that spans two creative worlds: as a singer-songwriter, his music has been featured in Top 10 Netflix series including Love Is Blind and Temptation Island, distributed through Universal Music and Virgin Music, and he recently signed a publishing deal with Bella Figura Music/Sony. As a poet, he has amassed over 100,000 followers on TikTok who followed the journey of this book to its release.
 Join us for an evening that brings Dylan Lloyd back to the neighborhood that shaped him
 Registration strongly encouraged, pizza and pop will be served. 
 The first 10 people to arrive will receive a signed copy of Coffee Walk Poetry

title: Psycroptic, Inferi, Cognitive, Summoning The Lich, Burned In Effigy
description:
PSYCROPTIC
Isolation can often result in unique outcomes. Hailing from the tiny, frosty, untamed and detached Australian state that is Tasmania, Psycroptic have become an unparalleled act in an enigmatic world wide movement commonly known as death metal. Fifteen years have passed since their formation in 1999, the band having released five critically acclaimed studio albums, all which show an organic progression along a clandestine path from which they will never stray.
On the eve of their sixth full-length, though more technical and brutally intuitive than ever, the four-piece has not been afraid to get in touch with their softer side. Long known as the ‘Tasmanian devils’, they recently became the first band in the world to adopt their own Tasmanian Devil, whom they dubbed Psycro, in an attempt to help preserve the critically endangered carnivorous marsupial. Newer elements too can be expected when the new album is finally unleashed – more vocal variation, a heightened handle on instrumental melody, and an overwhelming sense that this act has truly mastered their craft.
Psycroptic have toured all corners of the globe with names that need no introduction to those in the know – Cannibal Corpse, Suicide Silence, Decapitated, The Faceless, Obituary, Carcass, Nile, The Black Dahlia Murder, Origin, Kataklysm, Aborted, Despised Icon, Suffocation, Veil of Maya, Cryptopsy, Misery Index, Vader, Born of Osiris, Hate Eternal you get the picture right? They also recently guest hosted the ABC music video program Rage, an honour reserved for only the most class Australian acts. Metal legend Max Cavalera has also been sporting the band’s merch in recent promotional photos, bringing things full circle from the days when they were influenced by Sepultura in their youth. It’s safe to say that Psycroptic’s place in the history of heavy metal is solidified, and that everything that happens from here on in is simply a bonus
INFERI
Inferi is an American melodic death metal band forged from the bowels of Nashville, Tennessee. The band formed in 2006 and strived to merge the classic melodic metal sound with a taste of crushing technicality.
COGNITIVE
After releasing an EP and full length, COGNITIVE signed to Unique Leader Records in 2016 and released their album Deformity, which showed the bands dedication to their craft within a tale about their home states own legend about the Jersey Devil. Ramping up their tour schedule, the band continued to write and push themselves within the genre with technicality, speed, brutality, and songwriting, which came to shine through even more on the 2018 release Matricide, which displayed more focused effort while increasing speed and technicality even more. The band wasted no time in their touring schedule and hit the road supporting Fit for an Autopsy, Rivers of Nihil, Through the Eyes of the Dead, Vulvodynia, Lorna Shore and others, along with an appearance at Maryland Deathfest. COGNITIVE has become a touring machine with one goal in mind – always move forward.
Now with the release of their new album Malevolent Thoughts of a Hastened Extinction, the band has displayed more diversity and song writing more than ever, and proves yet again they are never scared to explore new concepts musically and explore new territory.
Now signed to Metal Blade Records in 2022, Cognitive is not only touring for their last record, but writing their next slab of brutality.
SUMMONING THE LICH
Taking inspiration from the best elements of Lord of the Rings, Magic The Gathering, Dungeons & Dragons, and Adventure Time, and wrapping it up in a fantastical death metal parcel, SUMMONING THE LICH has an attention to detail and commitment to storytelling that is second to none. United In Chaos tells the tale of the rise of the Lich and fall of the Kingdom Rodor – and the spread of his wicked influence across the land as his power grows.
SUMMONING THE LICH’s debut album follows a well-received, self-titled demo and live dates alongside heavy-hitters such as Origin, Beneath The Massacre, and several stops on the Summer Slaughter tour. Having honed their craft, they entered Sicktones Studios studio with producer Jack Daniels in Cape Girardeau, Missouri in September 2019. With mastering completed by John Douglass, the result is a technical, abrasive journey through fantasy-driven, modern death metal.
On United In Chaos, SUMMONING THE LICH haven’t just championed a fantasy world, they’ve created one in their own vision; this release marking merely the first chapter in a trilogy of albums that explores the outer limits of their imaginations. By inserting their storytelling chops into songs crammed with memorable hooks and meaty riffs, SUMMONING THE LICH have invited listeners to roll the dice and join the adventure.

title: 1st Set With Mario Abney
description:
As a Chicago native, Mario Abney’s trumpet playing fuses traditional and extended techniques in an inventive way. His uniquely personal vision for music endows it with an infinite array of tonal colors. He is recognized for his ability to create pure musical dialogues and hear music in a universally spiritual way. These qualities make him one of New Orleans’ most pioneering young jazz musicians.
Trumpeter, composer and bandleader Mario Abney’s musical career began at age 7 when he was introduced to the piano by his uncle Arthur. Influenced by both his uncle’s playing and the musical background of his church, Abney developed a love and fascination for music that grew throughout his years in high school. It was during this time that his interest turned from piano and drums to wind instruments; however, he continued to hone his percussion skills by playing drums for church services.
Mario’s first encounter with jazz was when he heard the sounds of trumpeter Wynton Marsalis. This sparked a fascination and soon Mario began to explore music by Louis Armstrong, Dizzy Gillespie, Miles Davis and other great trumpet players who established this genre.
Fast forwarding to 2024, Mario Abney is once again gracing the stages of his beloved hometown Chicago. From iconic venues to up-and-coming spots, he’s become a regular feature with fans eagerly anticipating each and every performance.

description:
Insight Meditation is based on the early Buddhist teachings found in the Pali Canon and forms the basis for contemporary secular mindfulness practices. The group meets for 90 minutes, which includes instructions and chanting, sitting and walking meditation, and talks and discussions that illuminate the key teachings on meditation and insight. The meditations focus on developing tranquility (Samadhi), insight (Vipassana), and Lovingkindness (Metta). No prior experience necessary. 
 The weekly meditation is usually led by Jon Aaron, who has been teaching in the Insight tradition for over 20 years at New York Insight and other communities. He is also a certified teacher and teacher trainer in Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction.

title: Josh Grau, "The Brand GPA"
description:
About the Book:
If your customers could give you a grade, do you know what it would be?
Odds are it would be different—potentially very different—than how you would grade the brand yourself.
Internal teams spend a lot of time hustling to develop KPIs each quarter. But those processes are rarely connected to one another, and nobody's grading on the same rubric. Worse, teams score themselves—which is like grading your own exam. Meanwhile, your customers evaluate you on a completely different set of criteria.
That's where The Brand GPA comes in. It's a new way to measure the health of your brand through the lens of the customer experience—while also redefining what brand should mean. Because here's the uncomfortable truth: brand has a brand perception problem.
Too often the term gets unfairly reduced to expensive Super Bowl ads or a logo refresh. But the most successful brands understand that brand is everything—from the product and experience they deliver to the way they communicate to the values they exhibit. So if your internal numbers give you an A but your customers' actions give you a C, you've got a serious brand problem.
145 Brands. 5 Subjects. 1 Framework.
The Brand GPA gives leaders—from CMOs to CPOs to CEOs—a customer-first alternative to the quarterly KPI scramble: a weighted, evidence-based framework that measures a brand the way customers experience it. It's a brand health diagnostic, a strategic planning framework, and a common language for your entire organization—rolled into one score that's easy to track, defend, and act on.
And as AI continues to change the game, The Brand GPA gives you a framework for harnessing it the right way so you can stay locked in and study the one thing that matters most: making the grade with your customers.
About the Author:
Josh Grau has spent more than two decades working with some of the world’s most iconic brands.
As an early executive at YouTube and Twitter, he helped usher in new paradigms—online video and social media—that fundamentally changed culture and how companies and customers interact. As a four-time CMO at companies such as Wealthfront and Yext, he’s brought his sometimes-contrarian approach to the C-suite, repositioning those brands to realize their full potential.
His breadth of experience gives him a unique perspective: no matter the industry—and no matter what technological shifts occur—the customer’s perspective is the same. They want a great brand experience, every time.
Josh splits his time between Austin, Texas, and San Francisco. He has taught graduate-level product marketing, brand strategy, and business storytelling courses at Northwestern and Stanford, and he writes weekly on Substack at Shades of Grau, where brands, people, and culture get put into sharper focus.

title: An Evening with Andrew Norman Wilson
description:
Andrew Norman Wilson is a writer, director, and artist based in New York. His first work of video art, Workers Leaving the Googleplex, went viral and was recently exhibited in MoMA’s main collection gallery for over two years. His first narrative short, In the Air Tonight, went viral and premiered in competition at the Sundance Film Festival. His first magazine essay, “It’s Not What the World Needs Right Now,” went viral and led to his signing with CAA.
 His films have premiered at Sundance, the New York Film Festival, and Rotterdam. His work is in collections such as the Museum of Modern Art New York, Whitney Museum of American Art, The Getty Museum, and The Centre Pompidou, and he has exhibited at LUMA Arles, MoMA PS1, and the Gwangju and Berlin Biennials. He has taught at UCLA, SAIC, and Cooper Union, and lectured at Oxford University, Cambridge University, Harvard University, and Yale University. He is currently in development on a commercial film titled Interlaken, a romantic thriller set in the Swiss Alps.
 Presented in partnership with the University of Chicago’s Department of Visual Arts and DOCUMENT, a contemporary art gallery in Lisbon and Chicago, the Film Studies Center presents a selection of Wilson’s work: a collection of deeply uncanny and often hilarious ruminations on virality, temporality, labor, and the ephemeral quality of human connection in the digital age. The films will screen with Wilson in person for a post-show Q&A. This screening will serve as a precursor to Wilson’s gallery opening at DOCUMENT on Friday, 11/13: Plump Caruncles Rippling Dewlaps Dangling Snoods and Sumptuous Plumage with Piercing Eyes Sunken Ears and Shrouded Beaks II, a surreal documentation of turkey mating season. Final slate of films TBA.

title: YARN w/ special guest Terry White & The Loaded Dice
description:
FITZGERALDS NIGHTCLUB PRESENTS:
YARN w/ special guest Terry White & The Loaded Dice
$25 General Admission // $30/seat Reserved Tables Available
You might expect a band that calls itself Yarn to, naturally, tend to spin a yarn or two. “That’s what we do, we tell stories, live and in the studio, truth and fiction”,singer/songwriter Blake Christiana insists. “We don’t always opt for consistency. There’s a different vibe onstage from what comes through in our recordings. There’s a difference in every show as well, you never know what you’re going to get.”
Yarn’s ability to persevere ought to come as no great surprise, especially for a band that spent two years honing their chops during a Monday night residency at the famed Kenny’s Castaway in New York’s Greenwich Village. In effect, it allowed them to rehearse onstage, mostly in front of audiences that often ranged in size from five to a hundred people on any given night. 10 studio albums followed — Yarn (2007), Empty Pockets (2008), Leftovers Part One (2009), Come On In (2010), Leftovers Part 2 (2011), Almost Home (2012), Shine the Light On (2013), This Is The Year (2016), and Lucky 13 parts 1 & 2 (2019). The band then took to the road, playing upwards of 170 shows a year and sharing stages with such superstars as Dwight Yoakam, Charlie Daniels, Railroad Earth, Marty Stuart, Allison Krauss, Leon Russell, Jim Lauderdale, Leftover Salmon, Amos Lee, The Lumineers and many more. They performed at any number of prestigious venues — Mountain Stage, Daytrotter, the Orange Peel in Asheville, the Fox Theater in Boulder, the 9:30 Club in D.C, South by Southwest, the Strawberry Festival, Rhythm and Roots, Meadowgrass, Floydfest and so much more, eventually surpassing 1,000 shows, half a million miles and performances in nearly every state. They’ve driven nonstop, made countless radio station appearances, driven broken-down RVs and watched as their van caught fire. They’ve paid their dues and then some, looking forward even as they were forced to glance behind.
Indeed, the accolades piled up quickly along the way. They have landed on the Grammy ballot 4 times, garnered nods from the Americana Music Association, placed top five on both Radio and Records and the AMA album charts, garnered airplay on Sirius XM, iTunes, Pandora, CNN, and CMT, been streamed millions of times on Spotify, Apple Music, and Amazon, and also accorded the “Download of the Day” from Rolling Stone. Shine the Light On found shared songwriting credits with John Oates (the Oates of Hall & Oates fame), and when audiences expressed their admiration, it brought the band a populist cult following of diehard devotees, popularly known as “the Yarmy."
Grab dinner before the show at BABYGOLD BARBECUE (link to restaurant website)
Or enjoy full service dining inside the club when doors open.
***PARKING***
There is rather limited street parking in the area, we recommend arriving by rideshare, bicycle, or rickshaw.
***AGE RESTRICTIONS***
21+, minors admitted with guardian

Chicago Metalcore est. 2025
“Beneath the Surface” EP available on all streaming platforms
MEL SENESE
Mel Senese is an alt-rock artist whose sound captures the fiery energy of Paramore and dynamic edge of No Doubt. Her music delves into life’s struggles, offering an inspiring and empowering perspective delivered with confidence. Mel’s honesty and electrifying performances resonate with listeners seeking both catharsis and motivation.
Beyond her music, Mel is a devoted bird enthusiast. Her conure, Benji, frequently makes appearances on her social media, charming fans with his playful antics. This love for parrots even influences her branding, with a bird-inspired logo that reflects her personality and creative free spirit.
Mel has performed extensively across the Midwest, earning recognition as Chicago Big Break Champion in 2017 and opening for national acts like Dorothy and The Veronicas. When not releasing music, she continues to perform regularly throughout the region.
In 2020, Mel embraced live streaming to connect with fans during the pandemic. Her engaging weekly streams garnered a dedicated following, earning her features in the Chicago Tribune and a TV appearance on ABC7. That same year, she collaborated with Bliss Skincare on a TikTok campaign, co-writing the song “This Is Bliss.” The campaign achieved over 7 billion views, driving massive success for the brand.
Coming back from a 2 year song release hiatus, Mel dropped a handful of singles in 2024, ending with the 5 song EP Called Main Character. It’s a celebration of self-confidence, resilience, and creative rebirth. The EP concludes with its namesake, Main Character, a powerful track that ties everything together. This song is about prioritizing self-care, setting boundaries, and owning your story. With its strong message of self-respect and empowerment, it’s the perfect closing note to a transformative journey in preparation for what’s to come next for Mel.

title: Boom!
description:

Joseph Losey
WRITTEN BY
Tennessee Williams
STARRING
Elizabeth Taylor,

Noël Coward
Hollywood's favorite pair of mismatched lovers, Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton, made eleven films together, and Boom! counts among the kookiest. In veteran director Joseph Losey's adaptation of the Tennessee Williams play The Milk Train Doesn't Stop Here Anymore, Taylor plays Flora Goforth, a wealthy, dying woman living in solitude in an island villa. She spends her days on a liquid diet, tossing displeasing items off the nearby cliffs, abusing her staff, and dictating her life story over an intercom system that pumps her memories and madness into every room. When a mysterious visitor (Burton) appears, she becomes convinced he will bring about her demise. Boom! is a feast of exploded art direction, extravagant costumes, and freakish rich-people behavior — it's as if the Taylor of 1963's Cleopatra stuffed her best headdresses and jewels into a suitcase and hightailed it to Capri with death hot on her heels. It never, ever lets up, and it's a joy to behold. A critical and financial failure, the film attracted supporters who were nevertheless a "quality over quantity" bunch. Tennessee Williams himself considered it one of the greatest adaptations of his work, and John Waters called it "the best failed art film ever, so genuinely beautiful and awful that it's perfect." The magic of the film even affected Taylor herself, who kept trying to purchase the island villa, only to be told repeatedly that it wasn't available (because it wasn't a real house). (Text courtesy of Chicago Film Society)
35mm IB Technicolor print from Universal
Preceded by: Elizabeth Taylor trailer reel – 10 min – 35mm

title: Realigning with Nature: A Conversation with MacArthur Fellows
address: 111 E. Wacker Dr., Suite 1321, Chicago, IL, 60601
description:
Join us for a conversation with MacArthur Fellows Jeanne Gang, J. Drew Lanham and Elizabeth Turk on how art, design and literature can help create healthier habitats for people and wildlife.
David Rubenstein Treehouse at Harvard University. Photo by Jason O’Rear, courtesy of Studio Gang.
How can art, design and literature deepen connections between people and nature and help foster flourishing habitats for all?
MacArthur Fellows Jeanne Gang, J. Drew Lanham and Elizabeth Turk will explore this question through conversations about how cultural narratives shape the ways people respond to the natural world, how cities can support bird and other wildlife populations, and how creative practices can inspire community action for environmental change.
These themes connect to CAC’s ongoing exhibition, Flyway City: Architecture for a Flourishing Ecosystem, designed and co-curated by Studio Gang. The exhibition highlights approaches to creating healthier urban habitats and addressing bird collisions with building glass, a problem that kills more than 1 billion birds each year in the United States.
Architect Jeanne Gang, founding partner of Studio Gang, designs places that strengthen relationships among people, communities, and the natural environment. She is a leading practitioner and advocate for bird-safe design and improving biodiversity in cities.
Writer, ornithologist, and conservationist J. Drew Lanham strives to connect ecological research to cultural narratives and lived experiences. His work situates scientific knowledge within personal and historical contexts, broadening how audiences engage with conservation.
Sculptor Elizabeth Turk makes marble works that explore fragility and resilience in the natural world. Her series Echoes of Extinction, created with the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, transforms the calls of endangered and extinct birds into sound sculptures that memorialize species loss and prompt reflection on coexistence.
Moderator Alison Cuddy is a Chicago-based writer, interviewer and cultural producer exploring art, architecture, and the natural world. She regularly leads conversations with writers and thinkers, among them Amy Tan, Margaret Atwood, Rachel Maddow, Al Gore and Michael Pollan.
This program is made possible through the support of the John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation.
Defying Boundaries: MacArthur Fellows at 45
This moment calls for creative courage. For 45 years, MacArthur Fellows have expanded the boundaries of possibility by questioning conventions, crossing disciplines, and driving collective progress. Throughout 2026, the Foundation is celebrating the groundbreaking work of the Fellows and inspiring public dialogue through a series of nationwide events and conversations.
Learn more at macfound.org/fellows-45.
Architect Jeanne Gang is the founding partner of international architecture and urban design practice Studio Gang. Known for a distinctive design approach that expands beyond architecture’s conventional boundaries, she creates striking places that strengthen connections between people, their communities, and nature. Her diverse portfolio across the Americas and Europe includes the Gilder Center at the American Museum of Natural History; a new United States Embassy in Brazil; and an expansion of the Clinton Presidential Center. A MacArthur Fellow and the Kajima Professor in Practice of Architecture at the Harvard Graduate School of Design, Jeanne has been named one of TIME Magazine’s most influential people in the world.
J. Drew Lanham is a cultural ornithologist, naturalist, educator, and writer using robust science, artful essays, and evocative oratory to color the conservation conversation. Guided by principles of interconnectedness and interdependence, Dr. Lanham’s work centers on the growing issues within environmental justice as observed through the multifaceted perspective of a Black Southern man. As a storyteller, poet, and passionate advocate for accessibility and stewardship, his writing is in praise of wandering and wildness and in protest against all not justice or joy.
Lanham is a Distinguished Professor of Wildlife Ecology and Master Teacher at Clemson University. He has received a MacArthur “Genius” Grant (2022) as well as the Dan W. Lufkin Conservation Award from the National Audubon Society (2019), the Rosa Parks and Grace Lee Boggs Outstanding Service Award from the North American Association for Environmental Education (2016), and the E. O. Wilson Award for Outstanding Science in Biodiversity Conservation from the Center for Biological Diversity (2020) and the Thoreau Award in 2024. He served as the Poet Laureate of Edgefield, South Carolina (2022).
A native Californian, Elizabeth Turk is an artist known for sculpture and through ET Projects, immersive art events. Turk received her MFA from Maryland Institute College of Art, Rinehart School of Sculpture in 1994 and her BA from Scripps College, Claremont, CA in 1983. She is a MacArthur Fellow, an Annalee & Barnett Newman Foundation recipient and a Smithsonian Artist Fellow among notable other awards. She has been represented by Hirschl & Adler Modern in NYC since 2000.
Launching ET Projects as a California 501(c)(3) enables Turk to develop social sculptures beyond existing art-world boundaries and make them freely accessible to the public. Through collaboration with local communities, she develops flash art events around environmental issues. The recent sculpture series, Echoes of Extinction, captures the ephemeral; the sound of voices on the edge of vanishing forever. Turk’s compositions— these sound columns— translate the aural into the visual, building sound in a silent structure, giving individual loss an indestructible memorial. Immortality. The rhythm and richness to the patterns of each distinctive birdsong becomes a recognizable chorus as a collection of totems.
Alison Cuddy is a Chicago-based writer, interviewer and cultural producer. Her features exploring art, architecture and the natural world appear in the Chicago Sun-Times, Chicago Tribune, Newcity Magazine, NPR and WBEZ. She regularly leads conversations with writers and thinkers, among them Amy Tan, Margaret Atwood, Rachel Maddow, Al Gore and Michael Pollan and has hosted and created podcast series including Library for the People, celebrating the 150th anniversary of the Chicago Public Library. For over a decade she was a host and reporter at WBEZ Chicago and is the former Artistic Director of the Chicago Humanities Festival. She develops creative projects for various clients including the City of Chicago’s Department of Cultural Affairs, Hyde Park Jazz Festival, Illinois Humanities and Walder Foundation. In 2019 she was appointed by Mayor Lori Lightfoot to co-chair the City of Chicago’s Cultural Advisory Council and currently serves on the board of the Arts Club of Chicago.

title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
address: 3519 N Clark St, SUITE C301, Chicago, IL, 60657
description:
Even in his darkest films, Pedro Almodóvar never shies away from peppering whimsy and fun into his explorations of the fringes of the human psyche. With his 1988 classic WOMEN ON THE VERGE OF A NERVOUS BREAKDOWN, he delightfully flips that equation, resulting in a hugely funny and whimsical film that lightly peppers human insight throughout.
Actress Pepa Marcos (Carmen Maura, MATADOR) is, well, on the verge of a nervous breakdown. Having been abandoned by her lover, she embarks on a quest to reestablish contact with him, all the while navigating the stresses of live animals, answering machines, apartment fires, a girlfriend with accidental ties to terrorism, her ex-lover’s son (Antonio Banderas, PAIN AND GLORY), sleeping pills, and inquisitive detectives.
With his trademark color palette, dynamic camerawork, and a virtuoso performance from Carmen Maura in the lead role, WOMEN ON THE VERGE OF A NERVOUS BREAKDOWN takes the pain of heartbreak and wrings every last laugh out of it.

Fresh off a breakout year that has taken him from regional Queensland to the global country stage, Mack Geiger is returning to North America for his biggest headline tour to date.
The Australian-born singer has quickly become one of the most exciting country exports, following a career-defining debut US tour where he sold out three of five headline shows and performed at some of America’s most iconic country venues, including Cain’s Ballroom, Billy Bob’s Texas, and Gruene Hall. The momentum continued with Mack’s Grand Ole Opry debut, marking a major milestone in his rapidly rising career.
His breakthrough single “String By” has cemented Mack as a global country artist, climbing into the Top 30 on Spotify’s Viral 50 USA, the Top 50 on the Billboard Hot Country Chart, the Top 40 on the Global Country Shazam Chart, and becoming his first official US country radio single. The track continues to build momentum, as his first ever single to country radio, it is currently sitting inside the Top 60 of the Billboard Country Radio Charts.
Following the release of his latest single “Pouring”, Mack is heading back to North America for the When It’s Pouring 2026 Tour - his biggest international headline run yet. The tour will see Mack bring his signature blend of neo-traditional country storytelling, Australian roots, and modern energy to fans across North America.
From cattle stations in regional Queensland to sold-out rooms across the United States, Mack Geiger is proving that authentic country stories can travel anywhere. This next chapter marks the continued rise of one of the most exciting voices in country music.

 It’s 2011 in Upstate New York, and nine freshmen women sit in a boat together every morning at 6am on their collegiate rowing team, competing with each other up for the fastest times, lowest body weights, and most influential seats, until race day when they are asked to put it all aside and row together as comrades in one boat. When one rower secretly rats out the Coach for allegedly sleeping with a student and is seemingly rewarded with the best seat in the boat when he’s fired, her motives come into question– as does her position of privilege on the team. Over the course of their freshman year, All Eight examines how the world of collegiate sports drives these young women with varied power to fight to win– races, love, power– at the expense of even each other.

title: Donnell Rawlings Live
description:
Donnell Rawlings is a dynamic force in the comedy world, captivating audiences as a comedian, actor, and podcaster. Since the premiere of his Netflix special, "A New Day," Donnell has solidified his status as a comedy heavyweight, earning accolades from fans and peers alike. The special, produced by Dave Chappelle, is one of four Chappelle curated for Netflix. Speaking about Donnell, Chappelle shared, “I’ve been doing this a long time, and comedians like Donnell are not only friends but have inspired my own career. Anyone in the comedy community knows these names and knows their time to shine is long overdue. I am proud to be a part of this moment."
Donnell is currently selling out clubs and theaters across the country on his "Black & Mild Tour.” He recently joined Chappelle at Radio City Music Hall and has performed with him twice on SNL. His electrifying performances have included a standout appearance at the Netflix Is a Joke Festival, New York Comedy Festival and the MoonTower Comedy Festival – he also continues to tour around the world alongside with comedy legends Chris Rock, Earthquake, and Dave Chappelle including the Los Angeles Forum and the Hollywood Bowl.
Off stage, Donnell is making waves as the host of "The Donnell Rawlings Show," a podcast recorded from his home in Yellow Springs, Ohio. The show, available on five major platforms, has amassed over 8 million views on YouTube, featuring an impressive lineup of guests such as Andrew Schulz, Teddy Swims, Steve-O, Dr. Umar, Tony Hinchcliffe, and Rapper T.I. Donnell's enormous following and sharp wit have made him a sought-after guest on major radio shows and podcasts including Club Shay Shay, Funny Marco, Something Burning, The Breakfast Club, DJ VLAD and The Joe Rogan Experience.
Donnell first shot to fame with his unforgettable portrayal of Ashy Larry on the iconic "Chappelle's Show," and he proved his versatility as an actor with his critically acclaimed role as Damien "Day-Day" Price on HBO's "The Wire." Fans also applauded his roles in STARZ's hit series "BMF," HBO's "Winning Time: The Rise of the Lakers Dynasty" as the snarky Mr. Earl, — and he won the hearts of so many in Pixar’s blockbuster film "Soul," where he voiced Dez.
Donnell received the prestigious Redd Foxx Award from The African-American Humor Awards, a testament to his impact on comedy and culture. Born in Washington, D.C., and raised in Alexandria, VA, Donnell’s journey includes service in the United States Air Force, where he was stationed in South Korea and at Bolling Air Force Base in Washington, D.C., in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
While his career continues to soar, Donnell’s most cherished role is being a father to his 10-year-old son, Austen. Whether on stage, on screen, or behind the mic, Donnell Rawlings brings his authentic, unapologetic voice to every endeavor, making him a true icon in comedy and entertainment.

title: Hayward
description:
As part of its 25th Anniversary Season, The Gift Theatre is proud to present Hayward by The Gift ensemble member Netta Walker.
Hayward reimagines Hamlet and Electra through the eyes of Luna, who reveals to her family — on the day of their father's funeral — that his ghost has come to see her. Beneath the haunting, this is a love story: a daughter's love for her father, and the complicated, unresolved feelings he left behind. The story follows a family shaped by the trauma passed down by a father who served in the Navy during the Gulf War. Across grief, they reach for each other, trying, imperfectly, to come back together.
Developed through the Pearl Cleage Writers Workshop with Goodman Theatre and Remy Bumppo Theatre Company, and named a semifinalist for the 2025 Eugene O'Neill National Playwrights Conference, Hayward is exactly the kind of bold new work The Gift Theatre was built to tell.
Learn more about The Gift Theatre online at thegifttheatre.org or follow on social @thegifttheatre #thegifttheatre
The Gift Theatre is a storefront nonprofit theatre company founded in Chicago’s Jefferson Park neighborhood, committed to creating accessible, inclusive and impactful theatrical experiences.
Our identity is defined by intimacy, collaboration and a belief that live storytelling can inspire and transform both artist and audience.
What began as a spatial limitation became a revelation. For nearly 20 years, we performed in a renovated shoe store—Chicago’s smallest Equity theater—where audience members sat just inches from the actors. That intimacy didn’t just shape our work, it shaped who we are as artists. We’ve learned to lean into the vulnerability and electricity that arise when actor and audience share the same breath, both fully present in mutual emotional exchange.
At The Gift, we are only interested in work that is challenging and transformative —stories that ask big questions and risk discomfort in pursuit of deeper understanding. We delight in the dark humor and unexpected joy that surface in life’s messiest moments, reminding us that even pain can carry connection and light. We believe that every story, at its heart, is a love story—rooted in longing and a search for communion.
Our programming isn’t bound by genre but guided by character-driven, emotionally rich storytelling rooted in truth. Whether surreal or starkly naturalistic, each play we share reflects our commitment to creating spaces of deep connection—among artists, between artist and audience, and within our community.
Presenting this show during our anniversary season in Steppenwolf's 1700 Theater feels like coming home — many in the ensemble first met at The School at Steppenwolf, and those experiences shaped how they think about telling stories.
Hayward is made possible by a special gift from Show Sponsor, The Michael and Mona Heath Fund.
The Gift Theatre Company’s 2026 Homecoming Season is made possible, in part, by generous contributions from The Arts Work Fund · The Copernicus Foundation · Department of Cultural Affairs and Special Events · The Gaylord and Dorothy Donnelley Foundation · The Illinois Arts Council · Melissa Thornley Consulting · The Paul Angell Foundation · The Rabb Family Foundation · The Saints · The Service Club of Chicago · The Shubert Foundation, Inc.

The Diego Rodriguez Big Band (DRBB) is a Chicago-based, 19-piece contemporary jazz ensemble dedicated to honoring the legacy of Black American Music while exploring its continued evolution. Founded by drummer and bandleader Diego Rodriguez, the ensemble – which made its debut in December 2022 – brings together a collective of young musicians united by a shared passion for jazz and keeping the tradition alive.
Drawing from Post-Bop, R&B, and Latin influences, the DRBB presents a repertoire of original compositions and distinctive arrangements that reflect both the individuality of its members and a collective musical vision. The ensemble has performed at notable venues throughout the Chicagoland area, including the Jazz Showcase, Andy’s Jazz Club, Fulton Street Collective, Epiphany Center for the Arts, and Elmhurst Hall, along with festival appearances at the St. Charles Jazz Weekend, OQMS Jazz Festival, and Chicagoland Classic. The DRBB has also featured guest performers including Steve Wilson, Marques Carroll, Jeremy Kahn, Kevin King, Abigail Riccards, Victor Garcia, Tom Garling, and Kellin Hanas. At the heart of the group is a strong sense of community and collaboration.
The DRBB balances the power and energy of a full band with the sensitivity and spontaneity of a small ensemble, creating space for expression while still maintaining a cohesive musical identity. Beyond the bandstand, the ensemble is committed to inspiring the next generation of musicians through educational outreach and school performances, sharing an appreciation for the musical tradition while contributing directly to its future.
This concert is a fundraising performance supporting the Diego Rodriguez Big Band’s Guest Artist Concert Series, with proceeds helping fund future collaborations with nationally and internationally recognized guest artists.

title: Jason Bonham’S Led Zeppelin Evening
description:
Jason Bonham always finds himself at home behind the drumkit. From this spot, he has anchored the tempo for a myriad of the most legendary artists of all-time. It’s the place where he initially realized his destiny as a kid. It’s a tried-and-true safe harbor for the expression of his purest emotions. It’s a direct conduit to his late father and Led Zeppelin drummer John Bonham. Following stints with Airrace and Virginia Wolf, he handled drums on Jimmy Page’s gold-certified Outrider. During 1988, he notably accompanied Page, John Paul Jones, and Robert Plant behind the kit for Led Zeppelin at the Atlantic Records 40th Anniversary Celebration Concert. Beyond helming solo projects such as Bonham and The Jason Bonham Band, he appeared in Rock Star with Mark Wahlberg and Jennifer Anniston. Plus, he lent his talents to Foreigner, Little Steven, Joe Bonamassa, and Paul Rodgers. He held down the drums for Led Zeppelin’s 2007 reunion at the Ahmet Ertegun Tribute Concert—which set the Guinness World Record® for “Highest Demand for Tickets for One Music Concert.” The evening spawned the Celebration Day concert film and multiplatinum album, debuting Top 10 on the Billboard 200, selling three million-plus copies, and garnering a GRAMMY®. Other notable projects have included Black Country Communion (Bonamassa, Glenn Hughes, and Derek Sherinian) and California Breed (Hughes and producer and guitarist Andrew Watt). He joined Sammy Hagar and the Circle with Van Halen’s Michael Anthony and Joe Satriani. In 2010, he introduced Jason Bonham’s Led Zeppelin Evening (JBLZE), packing venues coast-to-coast and supporting everyone from Heart to Kid Rock. A spectacle of top-flight musicianship, arresting visuals, mind-blowing lighting, and emotionally charged storytelling, Rolling Stone hailed its “set of Led Zep gems that were strikingly faithful to the originals,” while Billy Joel handpicked JBLZE to open up a handful of dates. Ultimately, Jason remains forever at home on the drums.

description:
Minneapolis-based Kiernan's first stop on their midwest tour, with Chicago songweavers Beauty Saloon, Ester, Damsel. Indie music for the people.
Kiernan is the Minneapolis-based indie folk project of Laura Kiernan. Their music can be described as "sounds for when you're feeding the pigeons" -- in other words soft, spacious, and best done with others. Their latest single, "Small Part of Me" is just that, an ode to their friends. Named one of the Best New Bands of 2024 by First Avenue, they are currently on tour promoting their newest EP, "Take It." Here, take it--you're gonna love it!
Beauty Saloon is an alternative rock band from Chicago Illinois, fresh off of an over 3-year hiatus. Fronted by the band’s songwriter Mike Molitor (Sick Day, Sylvia Ivy), Beauty Saloon delivers a wild energy to their sets, perhaps attributable to having yearned for a return to the stage for so long. The band features a new lineup including drummer Robby Kuntz (Red Scarves, Old Joy, Olive Avenue), Ben Baran (Busy Bodies), and Brian Samuelson (Mydge). Beauty Saloon’s recently released the five-track “$25,000 EP"; their first album “BS” dropped in May 2025, and was included in Uproxx.com’s “Best Indie Albums of 2025” list.
Ester is the newest evolution of songwriter Anna Holmquist‘s music. This Chicago-based songwriter draws easy comparisons to the English folk-inflected tunes of Bonnie "Prince" Billy, Joanna Newsom, or even the poignant vocal work of Kate Bush, but brings an urgent intimacy to their lyrics that weaves a whole little world into three minutes and forty-three seconds.
Initially the solo project of lead singer and songwriter Christina Henson, the members of damsel. first came together as a supporting band for the release show of her debut album “soft animal”. After a year of performing and writing together, the band knew that this former solo project had turned into a full blown band - a labor of love that couldn’t be achieved without all five members. Made up of Christina Henson (Vocalist and Guitarist), Peyton Meacham (Vocalist), Dan Wanner (Guitarist), Mike Pitz (Bassist) and Corbin Wyatt (Drummer), damsel. is rooted in the love these friends found for each other and making music together.

title: 2nd Set With Mario Abney
description:
As a Chicago native, Mario Abney’s trumpet playing fuses traditional and extended techniques in an inventive way. His uniquely personal vision for music endows it with an infinite array of tonal colors. He is recognized for his ability to create pure musical dialogues and hear music in a universally spiritual way. These qualities make him one of New Orleans’ most pioneering young jazz musicians.
Trumpeter, composer and bandleader Mario Abney’s musical career began at age 7 when he was introduced to the piano by his uncle Arthur. Influenced by both his uncle’s playing and the musical background of his church, Abney developed a love and fascination for music that grew throughout his years in high school. It was during this time that his interest turned from piano and drums to wind instruments; however, he continued to hone his percussion skills by playing drums for church services.
Mario’s first encounter with jazz was when he heard the sounds of trumpeter Wynton Marsalis. This sparked a fascination and soon Mario began to explore music by Louis Armstrong, Dizzy Gillespie, Miles Davis and other great trumpet players who established this genre.
Fast forwarding to 2024, Mario Abney is once again gracing the stages of his beloved hometown Chicago. From iconic venues to up-and-coming spots, he’s become a regular feature with fans eagerly anticipating each and every performance.

title: Improvised Music Series: Chad Kouri & Ben Lamar Gay, Willis / Worthington / Naylor / Jesalva
description:
Chad Kouri and Ben LaMar Gay present an evening of sound and color. Ben LaMar Gay is a composer who moves sound, color, and space components through folkloric filters producing brilliant electro-acoustic collages. Chad Kouri is a Chicago-based working artist, musician, and storyteller interested in the healing powers of color, sound, and abstraction.
We welcome Ben Willis’ bright presence back to the Improvised Music Series after his move to Osaka, Japan in 2025. He will be joined by violinist, improviser, and curator Caroline Jesalva, experimental vocalist, sound artist, technologist, and educator Paige Alice Naylor, and composer, improviser, and SuperCollider electronicist Derek Worthington.
8:30 pm: Willis / Worthington / Naylor / Jesalva
9:30 pm: Chad Kouri & Ben LaMar Gay
About The Artists
Chad Kouri is a Chicago-based working artist, musician, and storyteller interested in the healing powers of color, sound, and abstraction. His mixed-race identity is mirrored by his multidisciplinary studio practice, which broadly focuses on color theory, visual communication, improvisation, radical joy, social justice, and community empowerment, as well as Chicago’s monumental history of resistance music, jazz, and the avant-garde. Using a wide range of skills and strategies, Kouri reminds us to stay curious and make time for play, rest, and introspection, giving us more bandwidth for personal exploration, grounding, acceptance, and empowerment.
Ben LaMar Gay is a composer who moves sound, color, and space components through folkloric filters producing brilliant electro-acoustic collages. An explorer of many mediums who has been called a “visionary musician” by The New York Times, Gay has found a form of creative expression that begins with improvisation and expands beyond the limits of any single genre. He has been a member of the Association of the Advancement of Creative Musicians since 2010. With more than twenty years in vibrant experimental music scenes, his talents have earned him residencies globally. He is a highly sought-after collaborator by some of the most influential artists of today.
Ben Willis is a bassist based in Osaka, JP. His practice is focused on collaborative trans-idiomatic improvisation. He often collaborates with dancers, multi-media artists, and technologists. He moved to Osaka from the midwest US in fall of 2025, and he has performed with noise artists, ambient and hip hop musicians, and butoh dancers across the Kansai region. With the experimental bassist Flagio, co-hosts the monthly collaborative inter-arts session, Alt-Classic Studies, at Environment 0g. He studied classical and jazz bass performance with Richard Davis, Diana Gannett, and Robert Hurst. He maintains musical roots in Detroit and Chicago, and in 2026, his Chicago-based improvising string quartet, heroes, interlopers, release their debut album, Gotta Do More. http://heroesinterlopers.com
Caroline Jesalva is a Chicago-based violinist, improviser, and curator. She studied music at the New England Conservatory of Music in Boston, MA where she developed a practice centered on contemporary, improvised and experimental music composition and performance. Her music continually concerns the experimentation and intermingling of violin and vox, finding an expressive home in many disciplines, including experimental theater, dance, songwriting, puppetry, performance art, classical music, and free jazz.
Paige Alice Naylor is a Chicago-based experimental vocalist, sound artist, technologist and educator. Through sound-making and performance, she investigates the dissolution of time and the breakdown of language with electronically processed voice, tape loops, handmade electronics, field recordings, text scores, poetry, and repetitive, layered production. Her direct and interpersonal approach creates live sonic environments which feel vulnerable and intimate. paigenaylor.art
Derek Worthington’s work integrates elements of jazz, electronic music, art music, and free and directed improvisation. His composing practice combines experimental jazz with polytempic structures. As an improviser, he uses a constantly evolving live processing system built in SuperCollider, focusing on improvisations with acoustic musicians.

title: All Eight
description:
It’s 2011 in Upstate New York, and nine freshmen women sit in a boat together every morning at 6am on their collegiate rowing team, competing with each other up for the fastest times, lowest body weights, and most influential seats, until race day when they are asked to put it all aside and row together as comrades in one boat. Crew would be chaotic enough on its own, but off the water, their coach shows up at their parties and drinks with them, makes lewd comments about their bodies, and is allegedly sleeping with one of them. So when one rower secretly rats him out for allegedly sleeping with a student and is seemingly rewarded with the best seat in the boat when he’s fired, her motives come into question– as does her position of privilege on the team.
Over the course of their freshman year, All Eight examines how the world of collegiate sports drives these young women with varied power to fight to win– races, love, power– at the expense of even each other.

title: Improvement Movement / Jalen Reyes
description: Doors: 8PM / Show: 9PM / 21+Improvement Movement, the social betterment campaign/prog-rock quartet/non-denominational cult from Atlanta, GA, have made a new record just for you and your modern day malaise. Its called Your Perfect Real Life, because, well, theres a lot going right these days, right? Arriving August 21, 2026 via ATO Records, Your Perfect Real Life is prismatic, angular, jumpy, and eccentric. Its sure to inundate your ears, corporeal form, and spiritual body with equal parts unadulterated bliss and realist catharsis, or, in other words, as much good as you can reasonably feel these days. Set in a world of chaos where the news seems to be perpetually recounting stories of planes falling out of the sky, urban wildfires, the uncanny nature of a southern snowfall, and schlepping ads that feel plucked from a sci-fi movie, Your Perfect Real Life makes an earnest case for embracing lifes relentless unpredictability. Animated by the bands baroque take on the angular harmonies of grunge, the records eleven tracks sprawl and simmer, enlivened by the Improvement Movements novel employment of dynamics, sticky melodies, four-part harmony, and a treasure trove of experimental instruments. If youve ever found yourself enraptured by the lush harmonies of Fleet Foxes, the theatrics of early Genesis tracks, or the candid intimacy of Art Garfunkel, Improvement Movement may be for you. Improvement Movement is a democracy, and so they say, things move slow. That may be true for the internal machinations of the band, but their output has been quite regular. Each member of the band, who have largely been eschewing definition, are songwriters and instrumentalists who have spent the better part of a decade in the fertile DIY scene in Atlanta, GA. In that time theyve been swirling, relatively undisrupted, in their own primordial ooze and rubbing elbows with folks from the no wave, punk, improv, and free jazz scenes. Atlanta is about as DIY as it gets, they say. Weve got some of the most killing musicians in the world all spread out on these kinds of islands of urbanization. Theres always something new. That said, the band hasnt been in Atlanta much lately; they were on the road relentlessly over the last two years, supporting Unknown Mortal Orchestra, Iron It was a gauntlet, trying to live day by day. There was no room for anything with too much premeditation.

title: Mike Wheeler Blues Band w/ Shirley Johnson
description:
Nicknamed the “Sweetheart 
of the Blues” by the staff at BLUE 
CHICAGO, Shirley has been gracing the stage here since the 1990s with her 
spectacular performances.
Like so many 
African-American vocalists, Shirley Johnson started out singing in church and 
then went on to embrace secular music. The Chicago resident, whose influences 
range from Mahalia Jackson to Koko Taylor, Etta James, and Ruth Brown, is a 
gritty, big-voiced blues singer who can also handle soul and gospel. Although 
Johnson has spent much of her adult life in Chicago, the Windy City is not her 
hometown; she was born in 
Franklin, VA and raised in Norfolk, VA. Shirley came from a very religious 
family and was only six when she 
started singing gospel in a church choir.
When Shirley 
reached adulthood in the late '70s, she pursued a career in secular music and 
made her presence felt in Norfolk's blues and R&B circles. She went on to 
become an opening act for Aretha Franklin, Jerry Butler, Z.Z. Hill, and other 
well-known artists who were passing through town. In the early '80s, she 
recorded some singles for two regional labels in Virginia and those recordings 
caught the attention of a man who was planning to start a label in Chicago. The 
aspiring record man expressed interest in recording Ms. Johnson and sent her a 
plane ticket to Chicago, but when she arrived in the Windy City she learned he 
didn't have enough money to pay for a session.
Nonetheless, she

title: Created Equal: The Premises and Promises of the Declaration of Independence
location: Regenstein Library, The Special Collections Research Center
description:
On July 2, 1776, the Continental Congress voted to declare independence from Great Britain. Two days later, delegates in Philadelphia finalized a document designed to announce and explain that act to readers in America and Europe.
 The Declaration of Independence asserted the revolutionary right of a people to alter or abolish a government, grounding that principle in the “self-evident” claims that “all Men are created Equal, that they are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights” and “that among these are Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness.”
 Over time, many readers have come to consider the radical philosophical premises in the Declaration as founding political promises of the United States. In doing so, they transformed an indictment of the British King and a manifesto of secession from the British Empire into an American charter of liberty, equality, and rights.
 But the Declaration’s meaning has never been solitary. From the start, readers disagreed about what its authors intended. Since 1776, radically different interpretations of the Declaration’s ideas have been put to different ends—from demands for the legal, political, and social equality of all persons, to claims for the rights of states to secede from the union, to calls for the revolutionary overthrow of the government.
 How did the Declaration’s premises become its promises? Drawing on rare materials from the seventeenth century to the present, this exhibition invites you to explore the document’s meanings in its own time, to consider contested interpretations across history, and to reflect on what the Declaration means today.
 Curator
 Eric Slauter, Associate Professor, Department of English Language and Literature; Associate faculty member, Divinity School; Founding Director of the Karla Scherer Center for the Study of American Culture; The University of Chicago

Visitors to the University of Chicago Library may obtain an entry pass by checking in at Regenstein Library’s entry desk and presenting a current, government-issued photo ID, such as a driver’s license, CityKey, state ID, or passport to confirm identity. Get more visitor information.

title: Multi-scale Biological Adaptation to Environmental Variability
description:
More information - https://www.nitmb.org/multiscale-biological-adaptation-to-environmental-variability
 Understanding how complex, multi-scale biological systems operate in a constantly changing environment is a challenging scientific problem. One important issue is that the relevant scales span separate fields of research, such as genetics, cellular biology, physiology, neurobiology, and ecology—disciplines that use largely different methods and experimental models. This is an important limitation because biological systems are inherently multi-scale and involve complex coordination across scales. Moreover, we currently lack the theoretical and experimental framework to understand the impact of an unpredictable environment on organismal and supra-organismal responses.
 Mathematical approaches will play a critical role in modeling and predicting the complex, often multifaceted effects of environmental variability on biology across scales. Adapting existing mathematical models and developing new methods to capture the multi-scale effects of environmental variability is not a trivial task, especially when we are only beginning to document its impact on biological systems across scales.
 This workshop will bring together 75 scientists working across the fields of experimental biology, mathematics, theoretical biology, and experts in complex systems to discuss the effects of photoperiod, temperature, seasonality, and other types of environmental variability on the function of the nervous system, on organismal physiology, and on super-organismal responses, such as those that occur at the level of ecology and population dynamics.
