title: Hayward
description:
As part of its 25th Anniversary Season, The Gift Theatre is proud to present Hayward by The Gift ensemble member Netta Walker.
Hayward reimagines Hamlet and Electra through the eyes of Luna, who reveals to her family — on the day of their father's funeral — that his ghost has come to see her. Beneath the haunting, this is a love story: a daughter's love for her father, and the complicated, unresolved feelings he left behind. The story follows a family shaped by the trauma passed down by a father who served in the Navy during the Gulf War. Across grief, they reach for each other, trying, imperfectly, to come back together.
Developed through the Pearl Cleage Writers Workshop with Goodman Theatre and Remy Bumppo Theatre Company, and named a semifinalist for the 2025 Eugene O'Neill National Playwrights Conference, Hayward is exactly the kind of bold new work The Gift Theatre was built to tell.
Learn more about The Gift Theatre online at thegifttheatre.org or follow on social @thegifttheatre #thegifttheatre
The Gift Theatre is a storefront nonprofit theatre company founded in Chicago’s Jefferson Park neighborhood, committed to creating accessible, inclusive and impactful theatrical experiences.
Our identity is defined by intimacy, collaboration and a belief that live storytelling can inspire and transform both artist and audience.
What began as a spatial limitation became a revelation. For nearly 20 years, we performed in a renovated shoe store—Chicago’s smallest Equity theater—where audience members sat just inches from the actors. That intimacy didn’t just shape our work, it shaped who we are as artists. We’ve learned to lean into the vulnerability and electricity that arise when actor and audience share the same breath, both fully present in mutual emotional exchange.
At The Gift, we are only interested in work that is challenging and transformative —stories that ask big questions and risk discomfort in pursuit of deeper understanding. We delight in the dark humor and unexpected joy that surface in life’s messiest moments, reminding us that even pain can carry connection and light. We believe that every story, at its heart, is a love story—rooted in longing and a search for communion.
Our programming isn’t bound by genre but guided by character-driven, emotionally rich storytelling rooted in truth. Whether surreal or starkly naturalistic, each play we share reflects our commitment to creating spaces of deep connection—among artists, between artist and audience, and within our community.
Presenting this show during our anniversary season in Steppenwolf's 1700 Theater feels like coming home — many in the ensemble first met at The School at Steppenwolf, and those experiences shaped how they think about telling stories.
Hayward is made possible by a special gift from Show Sponsor, The Michael and Mona Heath Fund.
The Gift Theatre Company’s 2026 Homecoming Season is made possible, in part, by generous contributions from The Arts Work Fund · The Copernicus Foundation · Department of Cultural Affairs and Special Events · The Gaylord and Dorothy Donnelley Foundation · The Illinois Arts Council · Melissa Thornley Consulting · The Paul Angell Foundation · The Rabb Family Foundation · The Saints · The Service Club of Chicago · The Shubert Foundation, Inc.

A Chicago premiere of the smash Broadway hit. 
In a co-production with About Face Theatre

Synopsis:
Usher is a Black, queer playwright who spends his days working as an usher on Broadway. He spends his nights struggling to write an original musical about a Black, queer playwright who spends his days working as an usher on Broadway. Lines blur, thoughts intrude, and soon he finds himself wrestling to break free from a very strange creative loop. 
This blistering, groundbreaking, Pulitzer Prize winning musical explores identity, race and sexuality through the lens of a young artist at war with a chorus of his own demons and inner voices on a journey towards understanding and self love.

description:
For nearly three decades, WHY? have thrived in subverting expectations. title: Steve Poltz
description:
A dude named Steve Poltz (me) in East Nashville wakes up one morning and gets a call from another dude in East Nashville named Dex Green. Dex says, “Hey man, you live so close. You oughta come over and make some music. Maybe we’ll document it — who knows, maybe it’s a record.”
Capturing me in a studio is like convincing a whirling dervish to stop spinning long enough to sign a bill into law. It’s chaos, caffeine, and accidental poetry — art colliding with microphones and commerce in a glorious mess. That’s how JoyRide happened. No seatbelts, no helmets. Just unsaturated, unadulterated art. Real humans making real noise in real time.
JoyRide is my 14th solo album (not counting the Rugburns records, live things, and bootlegs floating around). I tour nonstop, so I usually have to be tricked into a studio under the guise of “just one song.”
The record opens with “If It Bleeds It Leads” — my kinda classic mischief:
“I can never watch the news with you because you yell back — you scream like they can hear you in the television set.”
Then comes “Petrichor,” inspired by the beautiful smell after it rains. (I later discovered Phish has one too, but mine’s the barefoot cousin at brunch.)
“At It Again” follows, a cosmic co-write with my brother-from-another-meerkat Jim Lauderdale, featuring Bryan Owings and Chris Donohue (Emmylou Harris’s rhythm section).
The title track “JoyRide” feels like a warm hug after a long road trip:
“Free hugs, no shrugs, wrong drugs, bedbugs. Smiles, laughter, for here ever after.”

title: Andrea Gibson’s Love Letter from the Afterlife with Megan Falley, the Chicago Philharmonic, and Extremely Special Guests
address: 50 E. Ida B. Wells Dr., Chicago, IL, 60605
description:
You’re invited to experience Andrea Gibson’s Love Letter from the Afterlife with Megan Falley, the Chicago Philharmonic, and Extremely Special Guests. This multimedia event brings together film, live poetry, music, and intimate storytelling in celebration of one of the most beloved voices of a generation.
At the heart of the evening is the film Love Letter from the Afterlife which captured Andrea Gibson’s final live performance: a brilliant, brave, tender, and raucous poetry set recorded at Denver’s Paramount Theatre in 2024. The Chicago Philharmonic will perform Blake Neely’s original score live accompaniment, creating a deeply immersive experience that expands the poetry beyond the screen. The film was produced by the team behind the Oscar-nominated documentary, Come See Me in the Good Light.
Guest artists will join throughout the night, coupled with film and performances that will transform each stop into a living, breathing composition and a singular celebration of Gibson’s work. Threading the night together is Megan Falley—Andrea's wife, fellow poet, who will share intimate stories of love, collaboration, humor, and artistic kinship. Through Falley's narration, audiences will discover the relationships and moments of serendipity connecting each guest artist to Andrea's life and enduring legacy.
Part concert, part cinema, part communal celebration, the Love Letter from the Afterlife tour invites audiences to experience Andrea Gibson's work the way it has always been meant to be experienced: together.
“When I chose to name the show Love Letter from the Afterlife, I didn’t realize how fully I was describing what was about to happen. At Red Rocks, ten thousand of us arrived believing we had come to remember Andrea. We left feeling we had heard from them directly. Nothing can replace being in a room with Andrea. But for anyone who never had that good fortune, I hope this tour offers something I didn’t know was possible: the feeling that Andrea is still speaking, and speaking directly to you,” said Falley.

title: The Dead Bolts
description:
All cut from the same kind of cloth that gets used and thrown back into a drawer over and over again, the original members of The Dead Bolts found each other in 2018. In a manner some would regard as premature, having only practiced twice, the band found themselves booked solid in watering holes and Irish pubs around their native south side Chicago neighborhoods. It was tucked into the corners of these establishments playing extremely loud and not very well for 4+ hours a night, where the band would cut their teeth among swells of underaged college kids, just like them, that had flooded in to drink and scream the lyrics of the same set of songs every weekend.
When they each finally wrapped up their academic careers in 2020, they got to work on putting together their first full length album. The song writing wore a few different hats, with an eclectic mix of songs reflective of what music they were into at the time. Historically speaking, they might have picked the toughest year to record, but they navigated their way through a few different studios and engineers to sculpt and finish their debut LP, Pretty And Burnt Out released in the Fall of 2021. They sold out their album release show at the locally adored Schubas Tavern, and what ensued after that was 2 years of DIY touring the U.S. in the lead singer Eddie’s mid size SUV. After a few more successful shows over the years, they continue to independently tour but have since upgraded to a used 2008 Ford E350 Van that they lovingly named “Vancis”. Vancis is very important to the band.

title: 2nd Set With Pharez Whitted
description:
There are many moments that can define a man’s life and for Pharez Whitted, this is one of them. He’s taken on the new role as Chicago’s Youth Symphony Orchestra (CYSO) Jazz Director and Howard Reich at the Chicago Tribune described Pharez perfectly – “Few Chicago musician-educators are more qualified than Whitted to build the new band, for he commands a richly deserved reputation as a trumpet virtuoso, seasoned educator and irrepressible champion of the music.”
Whitted is humble with his legacy and his deep roots in music go as far back as the 1930’s in Indianapolis where the Hampton Family Band first began performing. His mother Virtue, his uncle Slide Hampton and the other 10 siblings (12 in total) laid the foundation with their self-educated and courageous father, Clarke “Deacon” Hampton at the helm. With that level of determination and talent, Whitted was destined to inherit the gift of music.
If you asked Pharez what inspires his music, he’ll say that the world needs hope and beauty and his compositions were created for that purpose. His music is for the people, to lift them up and inspire beautiful thoughts and a harmonious vibe throughout the Universe. One love, one Universal voice.

description:
Two 
calibers of singers exist in today’s music industry. There are vocalists and 
then there are entertainers. Laretha Weathersby is both. Her dynamic, effervescent stage presence 
is unparalleled and her sultry, wispy vibrato makes her a Blues natural.
Voted 
2009-2010’s “Chicago Blues Diva of the Year,” she belts out traditional Blues 
classics with passion and poise and delivers riveting renditions of timeless 
R&B, Soul and Top 40 tunes, all while captivating crowds with her jovial 
disposition and dynamic dancing. Known for her rousing stage presence, crowd members rarely 
blink when Laretha hits the stage, fearing they will miss one of her signature 
dance moves or the chance to chant along with the charismatic chanteuse.
Reigning 
from the Southside of Chicago, Laretha’s mother, a former Gospel soloist, 
detected her daughter’s singing abilities and enrolled the toddler in piano classes 
and encouraged her as a teenager to be an active member of the choir at the 
family’s place of worship. But it was not until the 1990s that Laretha began to 
cultivate a personal relationship with Blues music.
Emerging 
as one of the premiere female Blues vocalists in the City of Chicago in the 
late 1990s, Laretha has performed at such legendary Blues hotspots as The 
Kingston Mines, BLUES on Halsted and since 2010 is a spectacular presence here 
at BLUE CHICAGO.
Her 
debut album – Dance the Blues Away – is an eclectic mix of traditional Blues 
infused with remnants of contemporary R&B and Soul. The album reveals 
Laretha’s reverence for conventional Blues music while flaunting her fluent 
transition into contemporary R & B and Soul.
According 
to Ms. Weathersby, “the power of Blues music lies in its ability to relate to 
each and every member of the human race. People of all different backgrounds 
can connect with the universal concepts of love, triumph and tribulation, which 
are the very elements upon which Blues music is based. I consider it an honor 
and joy to incorporate that human element into my live performances and it is 
with passion and humility that I accept the honor and challenge of preserving 
Blues music for future generations.”

20 years after becoming a worldwide sensation, Bong Joon Ho’s acclaimed creature-feature THE HOST returns to theaters in a stunning new 4K restoration, featuring an exclusive conversation with the Oscar®-winning filmmaker.
Both thrill ride and poignant human drama, THE HOST combined state-of-the-art special effects with a gripping story, brought to life through a creative partnership between Weta Workshop (KING KONG, THE LORD OF THE RINGS) and The Orphanage (HARRY POTTER AND THE GOBLET OF FIRE, SIN CITY).
THE HOST follows Gang-du (SONG Kang-ho), who works at a food stand on the banks of the Han River. Dozing on the job, he is awakened by his daughter, Hyun-seo (KO A-sung), who is angry with him for missing a teacher-parent meeting at school. As Gang-du heads to the riverbank with a delivery, he notices a large crowd gathered, taking pictures and talking about something hanging from the Han River Bridge.
The otherwise idyllic landscape suddenly descends into bedlam when a terrifying creature climbs onto the riverbank and begins crushing and devouring people. Gang-du and his daughter run for their lives, but the creature suddenly grabs Hyun-seo and disappears back into the water.
The government announces that the monstrous creature is apparently the Host of an unidentified virus. Having feared the worst, Gang-du is stunned when he receives a phone call from his daughter. She is frightened—but very much alive. Determined to rescue her, Gang-du soon makes plans to infiltrate the forbidden zone near the Han River and save his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host.

title: Madeon presents Victory Live
description:
“It feels like I just came home from a giant trip, a vacation somewhere. I haven't communicated pretty much in any way since 'Shelter.' I just saved up my story for the past three years. And I'm gonna tell it now.” —Madeon
Hugo Leclercq, the Grammy-nominated musician known as Madeon, first appeared to many as something like a teenaged fireball. In 2011, his frantic yet perfectly sculptural “Pop Culture” famously sampled 39 hits, live, from Daft Punk to Solange, instantly propelling the then-17-year-old to the international stage. By the time of his debut album, Adventure, in 2015, Madeon was a globally beloved artist with production credits for Lady Gaga and Coldplay.
Yet his first full-length, released via Columbia and his own popcultur, still evokes a bright sense of wonder about the world. “I very purposefully stayed with my parents when I made Adventure because I wanted to capture my life as a teenager in France,” he says. “Listening back, it’s a good reminder that it always works out best when you’re sincere. I wasn’t pandering, I was just really trying to make what I loved.” A FADER review called it “expansive, impossibly beautiful... one of the most radiant pop albums in recent memory.” Soon after, he teamed with longtime friend Porter Robinson for “Shelter,” an immersive, ecstatic single he calls their “victory lap.”
Now, a few years later, Madeon is perhaps a more deeply seasoned artist than wide-eyed dreamer from Nantes, France -- but he’s just as ambitious as ever. “I knew if I wanted to make something different, I needed to change my life around,” he says, so he moved to Los Angeles to focus the project in a new way. “I wanted to wake up in the morning and feel like every second of my life was about Madeon. My walls are covered with concept art and logo designs and instruments and references and records that I love. It’s all I do from the minute I wake up to the minute I go to bed.”
Good Faith is this radiant new era. The songs from the album are the sort of pop songs that, by any other artist, would have required hard work from a team of writers and producers. Madeon, of course, wrote and produced them himself. Following the path he began on Adventure with songs like “Home,” he is the sole lead vocalist on each of the new tracks. “I love to make that kind of music mostly on my own -- you’re not really supposed to be able to make it that way,” he says.
Madeon began working on first single “All My Friends” when he booked a studio for three days in New York “just to see what would happen,” he says. “I remember I was walking alone, and the sun was a particular shade. It struck me all at once, vividly. It was like a flavor: sounds and sights and smells. I felt impossibly confident and enthusiastic, and the song became like a premonition of what I had to do.”
Often, Madeon can seem as much a musician as a world-building architect, and there’s no question his full vision for Good Faith is shining through in high definition, standing as a brilliant statement of new purpose.
Good Faith, which debuted at #1 on Billboard’s Dance/Electronic Albums chart and received a Grammy nomination for Best Dance/Electronic Album, was released on November 15, 2019.

title: Created Equal: The Premises and Promises of the Declaration of Independence
location: Regenstein Library, The Special Collections Research Center
description:
On July 2, 1776, the Continental Congress voted to declare independence from Great Britain. Two days later, delegates in Philadelphia finalized a document designed to announce and explain that act to readers in America and Europe.
 The Declaration of Independence asserted the revolutionary right of a people to alter or abolish a government, grounding that principle in the “self-evident” claims that “all Men are created Equal, that they are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights” and “that among these are Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness.”
 Over time, many readers have come to consider the radical philosophical premises in the Declaration as founding political promises of the United States. In doing so, they transformed an indictment of the British King and a manifesto of secession from the British Empire into an American charter of liberty, equality, and rights.
 But the Declaration’s meaning has never been solitary. From the start, readers disagreed about what its authors intended. Since 1776, radically different interpretations of the Declaration’s ideas have been put to different ends—from demands for the legal, political, and social equality of all persons, to claims for the rights of states to secede from the union, to calls for the revolutionary overthrow of the government.
 How did the Declaration’s premises become its promises? Drawing on rare materials from the seventeenth century to the present, this exhibition invites you to explore the document’s meanings in its own time, to consider contested interpretations across history, and to reflect on what the Declaration means today.
 Curator
 Eric Slauter, Associate Professor, Department of English Language and Literature; Associate faculty member, Divinity School; Founding Director of the Karla Scherer Center for the Study of American Culture; The University of Chicago
 Visitors
 This exhibition is free and open to all. Visitors to the University of Chicago Library may obtain an entry pass by checking in at Regenstein Library’s entry desk and presenting a current, government-issued photo ID, such as a driver’s license, CityKey, state ID, or passport to confirm identity. Get more visitor information.
 Exhibition Gallery Hours: Weekdays, 9 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.

title: Time, Fragmented
description:
Time, Fragmented asks what it means for a place to be shaped by complex social and environmental histories, and how distinct but interrelated histories coalesce to create a collective narrative. Along these lines, the exhibition considers contemporary practices of unearthing, both literally and figuratively, and investigates remnants of times past, piecing together the story that unfolds thereafter. In the context of shifting regional powers and migrating stories, Time, Fragmented illuminates the (hi)stories foundational to modern-day Turkey, tracing diasporas of culture, thought, and practice.
 Materials entail historic postcards and photographs from the turn of the twentieth century displayed from a family collection by İbrahim Selim Ergöz. Additionally, building and ornamental materials from the Joel Snyder Materials Collection are displayed alongside photographs and maps from historic expeditions from the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Archives. Finally, multi-media works from New Orleans-based Turkish artist, Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes are presented alongside personal ephemera from the artist and curator. Through a variety of items from polyphonic sources, Time, Fragmented engages with the many layers of history—witnessed through a mosaic of lived reality, filtered through glimpses of past experiences—that live in time.
 Curator
 Time, Fragmented is curated by Defne Ergöz, BA/MA ’27, an Environment, Geography, and Urbanization major and Architectural Studies minor in the College, concurrently pursuing an MA in Art History.
 Artists
 Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes (Turkish, b. 1997)
 Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes lives and works in New Orleans, Louisiana since 2024. Türkoğlu Hewes is a conceptual photographer, building worlds for a single frame that carry the immaterial nature of emotions to a physical realm, portraying their silent dictate on lived experiences. The artist focuses on conflicting collective and personal agendas, evaluating dynamics between discipline and intuition, culture and callings. Her Turkish identity and upbringing rooted in strong familial ties appears in her recent work completed in İstanbul. The coexistence of culture and nature in her work criticizes the misconception of full control over emotional environments, similar to the power assumed over natural ecosystems. Türkoğlu Hewes studied fine arts, film and theater at Northwestern University. Her work has been exhibited in the 2025 Louisiana Contemporary at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art. She has been included in exhibitions at Soho Photo Gallery in New York City, Barın Han in İstanbul, and the Contemporary Art Center in New Orleans.
 İbrahim Selim Ergöz (Turkish, b. 1971)
 İbrahim Selim Ergöz, the curator’s father, currently resides in Westchester, New York. Ergöz has been collecting antique ephemera since he was fifteen, with a vast collection spanning his interests in historical documentation and postal items, especially as it concerns the Middle East North Africa region. His archive ranges from widely-available materials to rare collectibles. Time, Fragmented is the first instance Ergöz’s collection will be on public display.
 Support
 CWAC Exhibitions is organized by the Department of Art History’sVisual Resources Center. Additional support for the exhibition is provided by the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures, the Committee on Environment, Geography, and Urbanization, the Master of Arts Program in the Humanities, and Architectural Studies.
 The CWAC Exhibitions team includes Katie Chen, Scarlet Ding, Jiayi Laura Feng, Natalie Hsu, Grace Newby, Kseniya Portnaya, Stephanie Strother, and Yanlin Zhu.
 Related Programming
 Opening Celebration, Cochrane-Woods Art Center, Wednesday, October 21, 6:00 PM
 “Stories Objects Hold: Exploring (Non)Material Remnants of Türkiye: Curator and Artist in Conversation on Time, Fragmented,” Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures, Breasted Hall, Thursday, October 22, 5:00 PM
 Image
 Detail from Yeni Mahalle, Boğaz (Üsküdar, Bosphorus), postcard, 1908.

 CWAC Exhibitions is committed to accessibility for all our exhibitions. However, the second floor of the Cochrane-Woods Art Center is accessible only by stairs. To request an accommodation or alternative format, please email visualresources@uchicago.edu.

title: Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive
description:
Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive brings together album covers, book jackets, magazines, film stills, photographs, prints, and other ephemera featuring the work of Charles White (1918-1979) to examine the expansive cultural life of his imagery. Tracing how his work circulated beyond the studio and the museum wall, the exhibition reveals how White’s images centered everyday life and shaped a broader visual language.
 An artist who worked fluidly across drawing, painting, printmaking, and mural-making, White created what he described as “powerful images of dignity”, centering African-American experiences as well as historical figures and events at a time when such representations were widely distorted or excluded from mainstream culture. These opportunities for reproduction arose through active collaboration with musicians, writers, and filmmakers. White’s images were adapted, printed, and distributed across a wide range of media, crossing disciplines and communities to become part of a shared cultural consciousness.
 By foregrounding circulation alongside creation, the exhibition invites visitors to consider how White’s work contributed to the formation of a Black visual canon. His images did not remain fixed objects behind glass — they became living symbols, connecting people, histories, and communities through a sustained commitment to representation, relationships, and what White himself understood as a sense of oneness.
 Charles White Across Media: A Visual Archive is a special initiative of the Charles White Archives presented by Logan Center Exhibitions and the South Side Community Art Center. The exhibition is curated by Ian White with curatorial support by Paulina Alvarez, Jan Brugger, and jada-amina. Additional support is provided by the Ng Family Visiting Artist Fund, the Revada Foundation, and Friends of the Logan Center.

title: Anne Frank The Exhibition
location: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
address: 5700 S Lake Shore Drive, Chicago, IL, 60637
description:
ANNE FRANK: THE EXHIBITIONat Griffin MSI
Anne Frank The Exhibition is an immersive, full-scale recreation of the Annex where Anne Frank, her family and four other Jewish inhabitants lived in hiding during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Griffin Museum of Science and Industry is the first museum in the Midwest to present this exhibition, and Chicago is only the second U.S. city to host this extraordinary experience, featuring never-before-seen artifacts from Anne Frank’s life. 
Explore the world that shaped Anne’s story, from her early childhood in Frankfurt through the rise of Nazi Germany and the spread of antisemitism across Europe, to the Frank family’s move to Amsterdam. There, Anne lived for nearly ten years, including the final two, which were spent in hiding. 
Step inside the meticulously reconstructed Annex and reflect on the daily challenges, risks and courage of those who hid there before their arrest and deportation in 1944.
Anne Frank The Exhibition is a presentation of the Anne Frank House.

Join CBA and COS for this joint morning birding trip out to Crabtree Nature Center in Barrington. This destination is a favorite for many city birders who want to take a break from the hustle and bustle. The Forest Preserves of Cook County manages the property's prairies, woodlands, and wetlands that host 246 bird species throughout the year. This trip is designed to be a slow-paced, social bird outing.
Leaders: Sammy Cabindol
Pre-registration is required. Please contact Sammy ([email protected]) at least 24 hours in advance if you cannot attend or with questions.
Accessibility:
We will walk roughly 1.5 miles of trails with the first 0.3 miles of asphalt trail beginning on a slight incline before being relatively flat. The remainder of the trip will take place on mostly grass and natural dirt trails prone to muddy conditions with recurring slight inclines and declines and occasional obstacles including uneven terrain, roots, and holes. Dress for the weather.
Restrooms and water fountains are available inside the nature center building from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Cell reception is regularly available.
Weather/Attire/Other:
Comfortable walking shoes are recommended. Please bring bottled water. Dress for the weather. Based on the forecast, you may want to bring a heavy coat, gloves, and a hat. Ticks can be expected here. Long pants and insect repellent are recommended. Loaner binoculars will be available on a first-come-first-served basis.
The exact meeting location will be emailed in advance to registrants. Free parking is available in the nature center parking lot and driving is recommended.
Respiratory Illness Precautions:
COS supports the decision of individual trip participants to wear masks.

title: Sunday Somatics – Healing with Yoga
description:
This beginner-friendly yoga series features a heart-centered, healing slow flow practice intimately linked to the Smart’s How Do We Heal? 2026-2027 exhibition. Held in the museum lobby, the series features gentle movements and contemplative prompts that begin by exploring the various sources of suffering from which we might seek to heal—the physical, emotional, structural, ancestral—then move to methods and practices for healing. This 75-minute class culminates with aromatherapy, breathwork, and contemplative viewing of intentionally selected pieces from the How Do We Heal? collection. Class is led by certified yoga instructor Rhya Moffitt who guides practice with the intention of cultivating inner stillness, awareness, and presence. In collaboration with Arts + Public Life and Spiritual Life.
 Free; RSVP encouraged. Limited number of mats available.
 The first four sessions move through various sources of suffering:
 1. physical (health & illness): October 18th
2. emotional (loss, grief, and renewal): October 25th
 3. structural / collective (displacement): November 1st
 4. ancestral (trauma): November 8th
 The last two sessions get into the how with a focus on:
 5. wholeness, integration, (mind, body, and spirit): November 15th
 6. supportive healing modalities (healing objects): November 22nd
 Rhya Moffitt holds a RYT-500 certification through the Yoga Alliance. She studied at the Samyak Institute of Yoga and Ayurveda in Mysore, India, where she earned certifications to teach yoga, meditation, and breathwork. Her personal practice focuses on the Ashtanga yoga tradition, bija mantra meditations, and mantra chanting. In Chicago, Rhya teaches and programs community yoga events in conversation with the arts and healing work at Haji Healing Salon, Rockefeller Memorial Chapel, and Arts + Public Life.
 Rhya is also a Neubauer Family Fellow, Lindsay Dissertation Completion Fellow, and PhD candidate in the Department of English Language and Literature at UChicago. Her research focuses on Black anxiety, madness, and consciousness. Rhya views her yoga practice and teaching as a necessary wellness intervention that complements her intellectual work.

title: SOL Collective: The Voices In Our Heads
description:
SHOW DESCRIPTION: The Voices in Our Heads is a powerful and thought-provoking storytelling experience from SOL Collective that explores the inner worlds we all carry with us: the doubts, fears, dreams, memories, expectations, and conversations that shape how we see ourselves and the world around us.
Through compelling moments of humor, vulnerability, and reflection, the production gives voice to the thoughts we often leave unspoken. It asks us to consider which voices deserve our attention, which ones hold us back, and what can happen when we finally listen to ourselves.
Raw, relatable, and deeply human, The Voices in Our Heads invites audiences into a shared space of connection and self-discovery—reminding us that although our inner voices may sound different, none of us are alone in hearing them.
ABOUT SOL Collective: Founded in 2020, the SOL Collective was established to uplift and showcase the voices of women of color in the storytelling community and arts scene of Chicago. The name SOL holds significant meaning for us as it symbolizes our identity as women of the Sun, our connection to our ancestral spirits, and our commitment to sharing the Stories of Our Lives.

As part of its 25th Anniversary Season, The Gift Theatre is proud to present Hayward by The Gift ensemble member Netta Walker.
Hayward reimagines Hamlet and Electra through the eyes of Luna, who reveals to her family — on the day of their father's funeral — that his ghost has come to see her. Beneath the haunting, this is a love story: a daughter's love for her father, and the complicated, unresolved feelings he left behind. The story follows a family shaped by the trauma passed down by a father who served in the Navy during the Gulf War. Across grief, they reach for each other, trying, imperfectly, to come back together.
Developed through the Pearl Cleage Writers Workshop with Goodman Theatre and Remy Bumppo Theatre Company, and named a semifinalist for the 2025 Eugene O'Neill National Playwrights Conference, Hayward is exactly the kind of bold new work The Gift Theatre was built to tell.
Learn more about The Gift Theatre online at thegifttheatre.org or follow on social @thegifttheatre #thegifttheatre
The Gift Theatre is a storefront nonprofit theatre company founded in Chicago’s Jefferson Park neighborhood, committed to creating accessible, inclusive and impactful theatrical experiences.
Our identity is defined by intimacy, collaboration and a belief that live storytelling can inspire and transform both artist and audience.
What began as a spatial limitation became a revelation. For nearly 20 years, we performed in a renovated shoe store—Chicago’s smallest Equity theater—where audience members sat just inches from the actors. That intimacy didn’t just shape our work, it shaped who we are as artists. We’ve learned to lean into the vulnerability and electricity that arise when actor and audience share the same breath, both fully present in mutual emotional exchange.
At The Gift, we are only interested in work that is challenging and transformative —stories that ask big questions and risk discomfort in pursuit of deeper understanding. We delight in the dark humor and unexpected joy that surface in life’s messiest moments, reminding us that even pain can carry connection and light. We believe that every story, at its heart, is a love story—rooted in longing and a search for communion.
Our programming isn’t bound by genre but guided by character-driven, emotionally rich storytelling rooted in truth. Whether surreal or starkly naturalistic, each play we share reflects our commitment to creating spaces of deep connection—among artists, between artist and audience, and within our community.
Presenting this show during our anniversary season in Steppenwolf's 1700 Theater feels like coming home — many in the ensemble first met at The School at Steppenwolf, and those experiences shaped how they think about telling stories.
Hayward is made possible by a special gift from Show Sponsor, The Michael and Mona Heath Fund.

title: The Promised Land
description:
DIRECTED BY
Andrzej Wajda
WRITTEN BY
Wladyslaw Stanislaw Reymont,
Andrzej Wajda
STARRING
Daniel Olbrychski,
Wojciech Pszoniak,
Andrzej Seweryn
The rise of the industrial era and the capitalist boom it engendered are at the core of Wajda’s epic adaptation of the novel by 1924 Nobel Prize winner W. S. Reymont. The film charts the rise and fall of three ambitious tycoons: Karol, a Polish nobleman; Maks, a German hoping to improve on the fate of his father who ran a failing old-time mill; and Moryc, who appears to be disdained except for these valuable connections. Exposing the ways that workers are exploited for the sake of financial growth, the film builds to a powerful climax that connects it to economic conflicts that were simmering in Poland at the time it was made.

description:
Join us for a winter movie night in supporting local women in film with trivia & prizes from local queer-owned/positive businesses!
Featuring short films by:
NJ Hilton
Emma Page
Melissa Pratt
Farbota Lynn
Allie Morgan
Maria Spadafore
Mariana Duncan
& Jonael Leon Guerrero
Doors at 6pm and the event kicks off at 7pm.
Tickets are $15 in advance and $20 at the door.
Dorothy is 21+ and requires physical or mobile ID for all to enter. Dorothy is ADA accessible with elevator access on Campbell Ave. If you are a guest who requires elevator access, please wait by the black door with our logo in the window and call our staff to assist: 773-770-3799
Please note: refund requests are only available until 24h before the event (11/21, 7pm). No other requests will be honored.
------------
ABOUT THE FILMMAKERS
NJ Hilton (she/they) is a writer & director from Piedmont, South Dakota. She’s an alum of AMDA: Los Angeles. NJ focuses on stories of women persevering & navigating their identities. NJ is passionate about creating safe spaces in film for women & queer filmmakers; her debut short film “Late Bloomer,” currently in post-production, was a crew entirely of women & non-binary filmmakers. NJ’s next short film “I’m Sorry I Bit You In The Spare Room” is slated to begin production in the spring.
Emma Page (she/her) started her career as an actor, where she developed a deep connection to storytelling & character development. This passion led to her directorial debut with “Grandma’s,” a unique yet playful film that explores the relationship between two sisters on a journey to their grandmother’s house. Emma creates authentic stories that delve into nuanced relationships & their dynamics.
Melissa Pratt (she/her) Director of Photography, after graduating from DePaul University with a Cinematography concentration & Documentary minor went on to shoot a multitude of projects. Ranging from short films, music videos & documentaries such as Mission: Nepal on Fawesome TV. Melissa has also led a feature & pilot episode with Broken Bulb Productions. When not shooting, Melissa is a 2nd AC in Local 600. She’s worked on Netflix shows such as Monster Season 3, Saturn Return & Amazon Prime shows such as Barbershop & Paper Girl.
Farbota Lynn (they/them) is a Chicago-based writer, actor & producer with an interest in stories that question cultural convention while exploring the morally grey. In 2023, they co-founded Handkerchief Films & have since shown work at St. Louis Int’l Film Festival, Tokyo Int’l Short Film Festival, Desperado LGBTQ+ Film Festival and others. Farbota’s feature “Damage Ctrl” was a participant in the Chicago International Film Festival CIX: Development Lab of 2026. They are eagerly developing their upcoming psychological horror flick “The Lights Are On.”
Allie Morgan (she/her) is a writer, director & producer in Chicago, IL. She studied entertainment business at Los Angeles Film School & screenwriting at New York Film Academy. She has written & directed numerous award-winning short films & proof of concepts. Allie is the founder of Muffy Film Productions, which focuses on platforming marginalized filmmakers. She is passionate about telling stories for women, people of color & the LGBTQ+ community. Her ultimate goal is to put these underrepresented communities in front of & behind the camera in all of her films.
Maria Spadafore (she/her) is a freelancer in photo & video production as well as copywriting. She dabbles in writing, directing & photography. Maria graduated from Columbia College in Chicago with a degree in Directing. Maria has been working on independent projects as director, writer, assistant director as well as a production assistant on union television shows in Chicago.
Mariana Duncan (she/her) is a writer, director & producer based in Chicago, IL. She studied video production & communications at Columbia College in Chicago & has been a part of the Chicago indie film community for several years. Mariana takes pride in being able to bring stories of marginalized voices to life while bringing together a diverse group of people to make that happen.
Jonael Leon Guerrero (she/they) is a Pacific Islander producer & screenwriter. She graduated with a BA in Film & Television from Columbia College in Chicago. There, she began as a production designer & gradually transitioned to producing. Jonael has worked on numerous short films, including “The Love Doctor’s Apprentice” & “Fundraiser.” Jonael is a strong advocate for Pacific Islander voices & focuses on making stories for the underrepresented.

title: 1st Set With Andy Brown Quartet
description:
Bandleader Andy Brown has been one of the busiest guitarists in Chicago over the last two decades, leading his own bands and backing visiting jazz stars all over the city, as well traveling nationally and internationally with a variety of groups. He specializes in what he calls “old-school jazz guitar.”
The Andy Brown Quartet brings together four of the finest jazz musicians on the Chicago scene. Featuring Andy on guitar, Jeremy Kahn on piano, Joe Policastro on bass and Phil Gratteau on drums, this quartet combines the member’s shared musical inspirations and presents a lyrical and hard-swinging working band that has delighted audiences and critics alike. As a group they have performed weekly at Andy’s Jazz Club since 2012. Their Delmark records release Direct Call received 4 stars in Downbeat Magazine and was selected as one of the magazine’s Albums of the Year. Their latest recording is the 2023 release Good Atmosphere.
In a performance review the Chicago Tribune’s jazz critic wrote: “Inspiring music-making isn’t necessarily loud, aggressive, self-aggrandizing or heavily promoted. Consider what happens every Sunday night at Andy’s Jazz Club, where the superb but serenely understated Chicago guitarist Andy Brown leads a quartet. Like him, his bandmates speak softly but poetically. Brown’s pastel tones, softly stated melody lines and delicately rolled chords conveyed remarkable intimacy.”

Evolution can be ugly and beautiful, painful and euphoric. An Undying Love For A Burning World is the first new release from Neurosis in a decade, and a potent statement of intent and rebirth one that marks the first new steps of resolve and resilience.
An Undying Love For A Burning World is an epic album of colossal hypnotism beautiful, fearsome and utterly compelling in a way that only Neurosis can be. Aaron Turner (Sumac, Isis)joins the band on vocals and guitar, a name whose legacy is intertwined with the bands own and a true kindred spirit.
Neurosis have never been afraid of change, and here they embrace endless regeneration, surrendering to the emotional exorcism through heaviness and distortion that their music incites. Just as the universe tends towards balance, Neurosis cacophony of noise, rhythm and dissonance always resolves towards moments of beauty. The addition of Turners powerful vocals and wildly creative and unhinged approach to guitar proves to be a vital force as Neurosis find themselves again at the mercy of evolution and expression.

title: Kingdom Of Giants
description:

Since 1994, Subterranean has been a cornerstone of the Wicker Park live music & nightlife scene. Built in the 1890s, the historic structure at 2011 W North Avenue has a storied past, having once served as a brothel, a bathhouse, and as a wire room for gambling during the prohibition era. Owner Robert Gomez has worked hard to preserve the original features of the space that have been in place since the building’s creation and give Subterranean its one of a kind character, including the iconic Tiffany & brass chandelier that hangs above the dance floor. The Subterranean stage has played host to notable and legendary acts including Chappell Roan, Turnstile, Dinosaur Jr, Lizzo, Tame Impala, Charles Bradley & His Extraordinaires, Halsey, Pussy Riot, Built To Spill, Brand New, BADBADNOTGOOD, Lee Scratch Perry, Alabama Shakes, Durand Jones & The Indications, Fall Out Boy, and has been home to some of Chicago’s longest running residencies: Thursday nights’ Reggae Gold and the longest-running hip-hop open mic in the nation, the 606 Open Mic.

title: Making Movies, Intergalactico Sound Machine
description:
MAKING MOVIES
Making Movies is the Latin Grammy–nominated group led by Enrique Chi — born in Santiago, Panamá, and raised in the American Midwest — forging a sound guided by tradition, yet unmistakably its own.
The band has been described by Rolling Stone as “an eclectic blend of rumbero percussion, delicate organs, and grungy fuzz,” while NPR calls the project “perhaps one of the most unique groups around today.”
Their sound is anchored in the rich rhythmic traditions of Panamá and delivered with the force of a psychedelic rock show. Chi weaves the mejorana, a traditional hand-made instrument rarely heard outside of Panamá, into each performance.
Making Movies’ is collaborative across genres, working with artists from Rubén Blades to Kevin Morby, and David Hidalgo (Los Lobos) to Hurray for the Riff Raff. Most notably, Steve Berlin (Los Lobos) has served as a guiding force for the band — functioning as a spiritual band member, producer, and mentor.
New album Una Vida out Fall 2026.

title: Ok Goodnight, Snooze, Eve
description:
OK GOODNIGHT
Combining the talents of Casey Lee Williams (vocals), Martín de Lima (piano/guitar), Augusto Bussio (drums/guitar), and Peter de Reyna (bass), Ok Goodnight is an independent art rock band founded in Boston, Massachusetts, USA. The group formed when they were all studying at Berklee College of Music.
In early 2019, the band released their first single, “Rapture”, and later that year, their debut album, “Limbo”. In 2020, they followed up with an EP titled “Under the Veil”. Ok Goodnight self-released a concept album, “The Fox and the Bird”, to worldwide critical acclaim in 2023.
After three years of touring and writing, Ok Goodnight announced the release of their new album, “stop/go”, on June 12th, 2026. Their new material’s sonic explorations reflect a collaborative and multifaceted approach to songwriting. Through their unique use of sampling, live performance, and sound design, the group continues to push the boundaries of progressive rock. The album’s visual direction focuses on collages to encapsulate the eclectic nature of the band’s music, as the songs on “stop/go” aim to embody the ethos of mixed-media art.
To celebrate this upcoming milestone release, Ok Goodnight will play a string of shows throughout the summer at Mad with Power Fest in the US, Midsummer Prog Fest in the Netherlands, and select club dates in Europe. To top things off, the band will hit the road again in late 2026 to headline their third North American tour in four years.
SNOOZE
Snooze is an eclectic, four-piece math rock and progressive metal band based in Chicago, Illinois. Often jokingly or affectionately described by fans and media as “Meshuggah in major,” the band is well-known for weaving incredibly bright, happy melodies and rich vocal harmonies through heavy, polyrhythmic, and neck-snapping breakdown. Formed in Chicago, the group consists of four members who handle dense instrumentation alongside shared vocal duties.

title: John Mceuen: a Career Retrospective
description:
John McEuen, born in Oakland, CA in 1945, moved to southern California’s Orange County with his family for high school years. He and lifelong high-school friend Steve Martin both got a job in 1963 (in the magic shop) at 16! When, a couple years later, he saw Missouri bluegrass group The Dillards in an Orange County club, John’s life then headed towards his new dream: “be a traveling music man”. Leaving his Garden Grove spawning ground, his dream became more of a reality than imagined it could be!
Multi-instrumentalist McEuen (banjo, guitar, mandolin, fiddle) has been recognized as a founding member and award-winning outstanding performer of the Nitty Gritty Dirt Band. He departed at the end of the 50th year anniversary tour Oct. 22, 2017 due to demands for his solo work and the desire to do things new. In addition to John’s numerous solo accolades, NGDB was inducted in to Colorado Music Hall of Fame 2015. It is all covered in his book The Life I’ve Picked on Chicago Review Press, published April, 2018.
In 1971 John initiated the now landmark Will the Circle be Unbroken* album, hooking Nitty Gritty Dirt Band up with his musical mentors Earl Scruggs and Doc Watson simply by asking them in Colorado (brother Bill then asked Merle Travis, and it started growing) to record; it grew to inviting Mother Maybelle Carter, Jimmy Martin, Roy Acuff, ‘Bashful’ Brother Oswald, Merle Travis, Vassar Clements, and Junior Huskey, for 5 magic hot August days of recording. The now multi-platinum “Circle” is in both the Library of Congress and the Grammy Hall of Fame. * “One of the most important records to come out of Nashville” Chet Flippo Rolling Stone

title: Rockin’ in the Park
description:
Rockin’ in the Park 2026
Rosemont’s Parkway Bank Park Entertainment District is turning up the volume this summer with the return of Rockin’ in the Park, a free outdoor concert series bringing live music, tribute bands, food and drink tents, and fireworks to the great lawn.
The 2026 series kicks off on Sunday, May 24 with a post-show fireworks display. Free concerts continue every Thursday and select Friday evenings from May 28 through September 3, with Thursday night shows ending in a musical fireworks display.
This year’s lineup celebrates the sounds of Rush, Journey, The Who, Bruno Mars, George Michael, Steely Dan, Pink Floyd, Tom Petty, Led Zeppelin, the Bee Gees, Elton John, and more.
Concerts run from 7–10 PM. Admission is free. Outside food and coolers are prohibited. Parking is available at the Parkway Bank Park parking garage and is free with validation from any Parkway Bank Park venue.
2026 Lineup
Thursday, July 9: New World Men*
A powerful tribute to Rush, bringing the spirit, precision, and intensity of the legendary band’s live shows to the stage.
Thursday, July 16: Rod Tuffcurls & The Bench Press*
Beloved Chicago party band Rod Tuffcurls & The Bench Press delivers huge harmonies, sharp musicianship, and a wildly fun setlist built for singing, dancing, and staying out later than planned.
Thursday, July 23: Departure*
Departure recreates the look, sound, and feel of Journey, packing their set with high-energy performances of the band’s biggest hits.

Direct from Detroit, Live the Who pays tribute to The Who’s explosive 1968–1974 era with the sound, look, and raw energy of the iconic rock band.
Friday, July 31: 24K Magic / George Michael Reborn
24K Magic brings the Bruno Mars party with slick choreography, bold style, and hit after hit. George Michael Reborn keeps the night moving with the sound, moves, and charisma of George Michael and Wham!
Thursday, August 6: Brooklyn Charmers*
Brooklyn Charmers bring fresh energy and serious precision to the music of Steely Dan, honoring the band’s smooth hooks, sharp lyrics, and unmistakable sound.
Thursday, August 13: Echoes of Pompeii*

Thursday, August 20: Southern Accents*
Southern Accents recreates the music, style, and sound of Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers with contagious energy and serious attention to detail.
Thursday, August 27: No Quarter*
No Quarter delivers the full sound, power, and spirit of Led Zeppelin with a tribute show built for fans who want more than just the hits.
Friday, August 28: Bee Gees Gold / The Wayouts
Bee Gees Gold recreates the harmonies, look, and sound of the Bee Gees, from early favorites to disco-era classics. The Wayouts open up the garage with a high-energy tribute to 1960s rock.

title: Schnittstelle/Interface / ED/HF
description:
Harun Farocki / Renée Green · 25m / 33m · DCP
 ED/HF is a communion with Green’s colleague and friend, German filmmaker Harun Farocki. A dialogue that sometimes slips into monologue, the film is intentionally “blurry,” muddling the two artists' voices and histories. Interface is similarly in dialogue with itself and Farocki’s past, exploring the “cross influence” of juxtaposed images. In both films, uncertainty, fragmentation, and "blur" are essential to the construction of images and identities.

title: Soul Anchors of the Filipina
description:
Event Date: October 17 to November 22, 2026
The Filipino American Historical Society of Chicago Museum (FAHSC) is thrilled to announce Soul Anchors of the Filipina, a duo exhibition of paintings by the late Lea May Rivera, and collages and mixed media works by Marea Cordero.
Soul Anchors of the Filipina is a joint exhibition featuring the works of Marea Cordero and the late Lea May Rivera. Centered on themes of grief, memory, and ancestry, the exhibition explores the spiritual resonance and enduring strength of women across time and loss.
Marea Cordero’s work honors the Philippines as a matriarchal lineage, exalting female ancestors as the sacred pillars and enduring anchors of Filipino identity. Through the lens of ancestry and cultural memory, her pieces feature female ancestors looking back to the past while steadfastly gazing into the future, bridging generations of matriarchs who hold the community together.
In conversation with this collective heritage, Lea May Rivera’s intimate work serves as a personal sanctuary of remembrance. Navigating her own soul anchors as a Filipina-American, Lea’s art channels grief into spiritual restoration, weaving personal memory with ancestral roots.
Together, Cordero and Rivera transform grief into an empowering narrative—where memory acts as a bridge, ancestry serves as a foundation, and the Filipina spirit stands as an unwavering anchor across generations, distance, and time.
Written by Gracie Y. Essien
**Bring earphones to fully experience the exhibition.**
Mana Contemporary, Suite 316 - 3rd Floor Gallery (2233 S Throop St, Chicago, IL 60608)

title: Pearl
address: 3519 N Clark St, SUITE C301, Chicago, IL, 60657
description:
The allure of stardom on the big screen proves to be a road to some very dark places for Mia Goth’s titular PEARL in this stylish and gruesome prequel to Ti West’s X. With her husband away at war, Pearl finds herself dreaming of a way to escape from her boring life on the farm. She sees the silver screen as her way to find stardom and the love she so desperately needs, but her overbearing mother and her own dark impulses might hold her back from the fame she craves.
PEARL proves to be a delightfully perverse study on a standout character from writer/director Ti West’s tribute to ‘70s grindhouse, X. Its vibrant, candy-coated veneer plays wonderfully against the depraved desires of the main character bubbling just below the surface. Co-writer/star Mia Goth gives another deliciously unhinged performance as Pearl, a not-quite-innocent farm girl looking for love in all the wrong places. As much a love letter to the Golden Age of Hollywood as it is a demented look at the darkness bubbling just below the surface of rural America, PEARL is colorful, unnerving, and twisted in all the right ways.

title: Sunshine Boys
address: 10 S. Vail Ave., Arlington Heights, IL, 60005
description:
Sunshine Boys make their long-awaited return to the Hey Nonny stage, buoyed by a bevy of new songs and revived energy. The original trio (Dag Juhlin, Jackie Schimmel, Freda Love Smith) formed in 2016 and released two highly acclaimed albums before Smith’s retirement from rock music in 2022. Juhlin and Schimmel thought it was the end of their beloved band, but it was at Smith’s insistence that they continue with Gerald Dowd on drums. Turns out it was the perfect idea.
The group’s urgent, highly melodic songs earned them an instant following and glowing accolades — Big Stir Magazine named their debut album Blue Music Album of the Decade; legendary rock journalist wrote that their follow-up Work and Love was even better than its predecessor. Their new material takes the sparkling Sunshine Boys sound to even greater heights, infused with Dowd’s musical, muscular drumming and vocals. It’s a confident band, reborn and ready, with their stunning songs alive once more.

title: 2nd Set With Andy Brown Quartet
description:
Bandleader Andy Brown has been one of the busiest guitarists in Chicago over the last two decades, leading his own bands and backing visiting jazz stars all over the city, as well traveling nationally and internationally with a variety of groups. He specializes in what he calls “old-school jazz guitar.”
The Andy Brown Quartet brings together four of the finest jazz musicians on the Chicago scene. Featuring Andy on guitar, Jeremy Kahn on piano, Joe Policastro on bass and Phil Gratteau on drums, this quartet combines the member’s shared musical inspirations and presents a lyrical and hard-swinging working band that has delighted audiences and critics alike. As a group they have performed weekly at Andy’s Jazz Club since 2012. Their Delmark records release Direct Call received 4 stars in Downbeat Magazine and was selected as one of the magazine’s Albums of the Year. Their latest recording is the 2023 release Good Atmosphere.
In a performance review the Chicago Tribune’s jazz critic wrote: “Inspiring music-making isn’t necessarily loud, aggressive, self-aggrandizing or heavily promoted. Consider what happens every Sunday night at Andy’s Jazz Club, where the superb but serenely understated Chicago guitarist Andy Brown leads a quartet. Like him, his bandmates speak softly but poetically. Brown’s pastel tones, softly stated melody lines and delicately rolled chords conveyed remarkable intimacy.”

title: Nate Manos w/ Shirley Johnson
description:
Nicknamed the “Sweetheart 
of the Blues” by the staff at BLUE 
CHICAGO, Shirley has been gracing the stage here since the 1990s with her 
spectacular performances.
Like so many 
African-American vocalists, Shirley Johnson started out singing in church and 
then went on to embrace secular music. The Chicago resident, whose influences 
range from Mahalia Jackson to Koko Taylor, Etta James, and Ruth Brown, is a 
gritty, big-voiced blues singer who can also handle soul and gospel. Although 
Johnson has spent much of her adult life in Chicago, the Windy City is not her 
hometown; she was born in 
Franklin, VA and raised in Norfolk, VA. Shirley came from a very religious 
family and was only six when she 
started singing gospel in a church choir.
When Shirley 
reached adulthood in the late '70s, she pursued a career in secular music and 
made her presence felt in Norfolk's blues and R&B circles. She went on to 
become an opening act for Aretha Franklin, Jerry Butler, Z.Z. Hill, and other 
well-known artists who were passing through town. In the early '80s, she 
recorded some singles for two regional labels in Virginia and those recordings 
caught the attention of a man who was planning to start a label in Chicago. The 
aspiring record man expressed interest in recording Ms. Johnson and sent her a 
plane ticket to Chicago, but when she arrived in the Windy City she learned he 
didn't have enough money to pay for a session.
Nonetheless, she 
decided to remain in Chicago and became active on the city's blues circuit, 
where she has performed both Blues and Soul. The musicians she worked with in 
Chicago included Little Johnny Christian, Artie "Blues Boy" White, 
and keyboardist “Professor” Eddie Lusk (who was a staple at BLUE CHICAGO and 
took Johnson on the road with him on international tours.)
Since the '90s, Johnson has made many 
recordings and in 2000 is one of the vocalists recorded on BLUE CHICAGO’s CD 
entitled “Mojo Mamas.”

title: Created Equal: The Premises and Promises of the Declaration of Independence
location: Regenstein Library, The Special Collections Research Center
description:
On July 2, 1776, the Continental Congress voted to declare independence from Great Britain. Two days later, delegates in Philadelphia finalized a document designed to announce and explain that act to readers in America and Europe.
 The Declaration of Independence asserted the revolutionary right of a people to alter or abolish a government, grounding that principle in the “self-evident” claims that “all Men are created Equal, that they are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights” and “that among these are Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness.”
 Over time, many readers have come to consider the radical philosophical premises in the Declaration as founding political promises of the United States. In doing so, they transformed an indictment of the British King and a manifesto of secession from the British Empire into an American charter of liberty, equality, and rights.
 But the Declaration’s meaning has never been solitary. From the start, readers disagreed about what its authors intended. Since 1776, radically different interpretations of the Declaration’s ideas have been put to different ends—from demands for the legal, political, and social equality of all persons, to claims for the rights of states to secede from the union, to calls for the revolutionary overthrow of the government.
 How did the Declaration’s premises become its promises? Drawing on rare materials from the seventeenth century to the present, this exhibition invites you to explore the document’s meanings in its own time, to consider contested interpretations across history, and to reflect on what the Declaration means today.
 Curator
 Eric Slauter, Associate Professor, Department of English Language and Literature; Associate faculty member, Divinity School; Founding Director of the Karla Scherer Center for the Study of American Culture; The University of Chicago
 Visitors
 This exhibition is free and open to all. Visitors to the University of Chicago Library may obtain an entry pass by checking in at Regenstein Library’s entry desk and presenting a current, government-issued photo ID, such as a driver’s license, CityKey, state ID, or passport to confirm identity. Get more visitor information.
 Exhibition Gallery Hours: Weekdays, 9 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.

title: Time, Fragmented
description:
Time, Fragmented asks what it means for a place to be shaped by complex social and environmental histories, and how distinct but interrelated histories coalesce to create a collective narrative. Along these lines, the exhibition considers contemporary practices of unearthing, both literally and figuratively, and investigates remnants of times past, piecing together the story that unfolds thereafter. In the context of shifting regional powers and migrating stories, Time, Fragmented illuminates the (hi)stories foundational to modern-day Turkey, tracing diasporas of culture, thought, and practice.
 Materials entail historic postcards and photographs from the turn of the twentieth century displayed from a family collection by İbrahim Selim Ergöz. Additionally, building and ornamental materials from the Joel Snyder Materials Collection are displayed alongside photographs and maps from historic expeditions from the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures Archives. Finally, multi-media works from New Orleans-based Turkish artist, Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes are presented alongside personal ephemera from the artist and curator. Through a variety of items from polyphonic sources, Time, Fragmented engages with the many layers of history—witnessed through a mosaic of lived reality, filtered through glimpses of past experiences—that live in time.
 Curator
 Time, Fragmented is curated by Defne Ergöz, BA/MA ’27, an Environment, Geography, and Urbanization major and Architectural Studies minor in the College, concurrently pursuing an MA in Art History.
 Artists
 Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes (Turkish, b. 1997)
 Deniz Türkoğlu Hewes lives and works in New Orleans, Louisiana since 2024. Türkoğlu Hewes is a conceptual photographer, building worlds for a single frame that carry the immaterial nature of emotions to a physical realm, portraying their silent dictate on lived experiences. The artist focuses on conflicting collective and personal agendas, evaluating dynamics between discipline and intuition, culture and callings. Her Turkish identity and upbringing rooted in strong familial ties appears in her recent work completed in İstanbul. The coexistence of culture and nature in her work criticizes the misconception of full control over emotional environments, similar to the power assumed over natural ecosystems. Türkoğlu Hewes studied fine arts, film and theater at Northwestern University. Her work has been exhibited in the 2025 Louisiana Contemporary at the Ogden Museum of Southern Art. She has been included in exhibitions at Soho Photo Gallery in New York City, Barın Han in İstanbul, and the Contemporary Art Center in New Orleans.
 İbrahim Selim Ergöz (Turkish, b. 1971)
 İbrahim Selim Ergöz, the curator’s father, currently resides in Westchester, New York. Ergöz has been collecting antique ephemera since he was fifteen, with a vast collection spanning his interests in historical documentation and postal items, especially as it concerns the Middle East North Africa region. His archive ranges from widely-available materials to rare collectibles. Time, Fragmented is the first instance Ergöz’s collection will be on public display.
 Support
 CWAC Exhibitions is organized by the Department of Art History’sVisual Resources Center. Additional support for the exhibition is provided by the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures, the Committee on Environment, Geography, and Urbanization, the Master of Arts Program in the Humanities, and Architectural Studies.
 The CWAC Exhibitions team includes Katie Chen, Scarlet Ding, Jiayi Laura Feng, Natalie Hsu, Grace Newby, Kseniya Portnaya, Stephanie Strother, and Yanlin Zhu.

title: Pierre Bismuth: Love Bless America
location: Neubauer Collegium for Culture and Society
description:
This exhibition features new works by the French artist and filmmaker Pierre Bismuth. The centerpiece is a long-form meditative film documenting a creative collaboration between Joshua Abrams and Sharon Udoh, two leading figures from Chicago’s jazz and improvised music scene. Bismuth tasked them with composing a 21st-century spiritual based on a lyrical hymn he wrote for the project. The film traces the magic and workaday practice of “inspiration,” taking the traditions of religious music as a point of departure for a multi-layered reflection on love, music, and the divine. In addition to this new film, Bismuth will present a series of digital images resembling American flags emblazoned with lyrics from the hymn.
 Curated by Dieter Roelstraete.
 The Neubauer Collegium Gallery is free and open to the public. Gallery hours: M–F, 9–4.
 The Neubauer Collegium Gallery is supported by the Neubauer Family Foundation and the Brenda Mulmed Shapiro Fund. Additional support for this exhibition was provided by Bernard Friedman, the Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, and the France Chicago Center at the University of Chicago.

title: Anne Frank The Exhibition
location: Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
address: 5700 S Lake Shore Drive, Chicago, IL, 60637
description:
ANNE FRANK: THE EXHIBITIONat Griffin MSI
Anne Frank The Exhibition is an immersive, full-scale recreation of the Annex where Anne Frank, her family and four other Jewish inhabitants lived in hiding during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Griffin Museum of Science and Industry is the first museum in the Midwest to present this exhibition, and Chicago is only the second U.S. city to host this extraordinary experience, featuring never-before-seen artifacts from Anne Frank’s life. 
Explore the world that shaped Anne’s story, from her early childhood in Frankfurt through the rise of Nazi Germany and the spread of antisemitism across Europe, to the Frank family’s move to Amsterdam. There, Anne lived for nearly ten years, including the final two, which were spent in hiding. 
Step inside the meticulously reconstructed Annex and reflect on the daily challenges, risks and courage of those who hid there before their arrest and deportation in 1944.
Anne Frank The Exhibition is a presentation of the Anne Frank House.

title: Diaspora Duos
description:
**Diaspora Duos is back!** Join BIYA BIYA at Color Club for a lively music series where artists from different cultures are commissioned to collaborate together. Steeped in diverse traditions, each specially curated Duo will present a world premiere set that showcases the two performers’ cultural roots.
**November Featured Duos**
**Hugo Flores García** makes music with guitars, computers, and found sounds, blending Latinx textures and rhythms with ambient and experimental forms across improvised and composed work. Hugo plays guitar in Chicago psychotropical band Cabeza de Chivo.
**Dr. Aliah Ajamoughli,** PhD is a Syrian American ethnomusicologist, cellist, educator. Her musical style intertwines seemingly two opposing worlds: the folk tunes of her fatherland Syria with medleys of her Alabama upbringing. This blending of bluegrass and maqam sounds the necessity of revolution, joy, and hope across global systems of oppression.
**Cruz** is a pioneering Chicago-based trumpet player, clarinetist, and educator redefining the landscape of regional Mexican music. A proud Southwest Side native, she pursued collegiate music studies and has performed widely across the city in jazz, orchestral, mariachi, and concert band ensembles.
**KASIA** is a Chicago-based Polish-American singer-songwriter blending various genres like jazz, bossa nova, Mexican boleros, Japanese city pop, and Polish folk. Having lived in Poland, Ecuador, and Indonesia, she sings in four languages, writing intimate songs about love, family, and feminine resilience. She's received a DCASE 2026 Grant to produce her first jazz EP Kocham Cię! (2027).
*BIYA BIYA produces Diaspora Duos with the following tenets:*
1. Performance intertwining two traditions and two local artists in a beautiful evening of sound and storytelling.
2. Playground for musicians to co-create something new; then inviting the audience to jam and experience it for themselves.
3. Platform to support Chicago’s local musicians keeping their respective cultures and the cultural richness of Chicago as a whole alive. By offering a guaranteed stipend for each artist’s time, access to free studio rehearsal space, as well as a professional multimedia package, feature on BIYA BIYA’s YouTube series and extensive concert promotion, artists are well positioned after participation in Diaspora Duos to gain a new audiences and market themselves stronger in the future.
4. Preservation of the evening’s creativity, and the musical tradition each artist brings to the series. By publishing performance videos on YouTube as part of a Diaspora Duos series, the new sounds created will be preserved, celebrated and revisited, while cultivating an audience beyond Chicago.
Presented by BIYA BIYA Productions.

title: Point Blank (1967)
address: 3519 N Clark St, SUITE C301, Chicago, IL, 60657
description:
British director John Boorman brought a European sensibility to a Los Angeles neo-noir: POINT BLANK is Antonioni plus violence, Francesco Rosi without politics. The title reverberates like a pun-point: blank. Lee Marvin is Walker, left for dead in an Alcatraz heist and now out to find the $93,000 he has coming. No more, no less, unless you count revenge. The trail leads to the City of Angels and the syndicate that runs it out of car lots and Santa Monica penthouses, the kind of places you know exist only with a little larceny. Picking up on the modern surface of his locale, Boorman takes a champagne-blonde color scheme to a hallucinatory degree, blonde on blond, like Angie Dickinson's bouffant and Marvin's silvery pate (here, we have the bad, the brunette, and the bald). Los Angeles is inherently horizontal. The payoff, visually and narratively, occurs in that storm drain affectionately known as the L.A. River, viewed from a bridge over imagined waters. (BAMPFA)
DCP courtesy of Warner Bros.

Rosemont’s Parkway Bank Park Entertainment District is turning up the volume this summer with the return of Rockin’ in the Park, a free outdoor concert series bringing live music, tribute bands, food and drink tents, and fireworks to the great lawn.
The 2026 series kicks off on Sunday, May 24 with a post-show fireworks display. Free concerts continue every Thursday and select Friday evenings from May 28 through September 3, with Thursday night shows ending in a musical fireworks display.
This year’s lineup celebrates the sounds of Rush, Journey, The Who, Bruno Mars, George Michael, Steely Dan, Pink Floyd, Tom Petty, Led Zeppelin, the Bee Gees, Elton John, and more.

A powerful tribute to Rush, bringing the spirit, precision, and intensity of the legendary band’s live shows to the stage.
Thursday, July 16: Rod Tuffcurls & The Bench Press*
Beloved Chicago party band Rod Tuffcurls & The Bench Press delivers huge harmonies, sharp musicianship, and a wildly fun setlist built for singing, dancing, and staying out later than planned.

Wajda’s EVERYTHING FOR SALE is a film-within-a-film about a director’s search for his leading man, who goes missing from the set. It was inspired by the tragic death of Zbigniew Cybulski, the beloved star of ASHES AND DIAMONDS who became an iconic cult figure in Polish cinema. description: A Gene Siskel Film Center holiday favorite, we bring back the ever-popular cult film by Hiroshi Teshigahara (WOMAN OF THE DUNES), inspired by the wild, undulating, joyously erupting forms of Barcelona architect Antoni Gaud. Teshigahara's eye for texture, shape, and sensual detail meets Gaud's whimsy in the cinematic exploration of such masterpieces of visionary architecture as the basilica of La Sagrada Famlia. The contemporary of artists such as Picasso and Joan Mir, Gaud drew on Barcelona's medieval Romanesque architecture and ancient Arab culture for his inspiration. This film reveals the intricacy and hallucinatory richness of his concepts through camerawork alone. Forgoing narration, Teshigahara accompanies his images with a brilliantly eclectic selection of music, ranging from baroque harpsichord to glass orchestra. title: They Are All Our Sons
address: 1333 N. Milwaukee Ave, 2nd Floor, Chicago, IL, 60622
description:
18+ ONLY
They Are All Our Sons is an immersive theatrical experience that reimagines one of our oldest myths, the Medusa myth, against the backdrop of a modern-day strip club. It's not just a play, but a tool for social change.
When two young dancers meet at the club, Athena quickly takes Medusa under her wing. The club encourages their bond, and soon they're sisters, dance partners, and the act everyone pays to see. But as Medusa grows obsessed with her own awakening, the power play between men and women, and finally healing from her past, she begins to challenge the stability of the only place Athena has ever felt in control.
The show moves through joy, resilience, pain, and rage, exploring the sisterhood wound and the systems of power the club operates within. We are left with the question: what if Medusa was never the monster? What if she was a woman who got labeled one because it was easier than holding a god accountable?

20 years after becoming a worldwide sensation, Bong Joon Ho’s acclaimed creature-feature THE HOST returns to theaters in a stunning new 4K restoration, featuring an exclusive conversation with the Oscar®-winning filmmaker.
Both thrill ride and poignant human drama, THE HOST combined state-of-the-art special effects with a gripping story, brought to life through a creative partnership between Weta Workshop (KING KONG, THE LORD OF THE RINGS) and The Orphanage (HARRY POTTER AND THE GOBLET OF FIRE, SIN CITY).
THE HOST follows Gang-du (SONG Kang-ho), who works at a food stand on the banks of the Han River. Dozing on the job, he is awakened by his daughter, Hyun-seo (KO A-sung), who is angry with him for missing a teacher-parent meeting at school. As Gang-du heads to the riverbank with a delivery, he notices a large crowd gathered, taking pictures and talking about something hanging from the Han River Bridge.
The otherwise idyllic landscape suddenly descends into bedlam when a terrifying creature climbs onto the riverbank and begins crushing and devouring people. Gang-du and his daughter run for their lives, but the creature suddenly grabs Hyun-seo and disappears back into the water.
The government announces that the monstrous creature is apparently the Host of an unidentified virus. Having feared the worst, Gang-du is stunned when he receives a phone call from his daughter. She is frightened—but very much alive. Determined to rescue her, Gang-du soon makes plans to infiltrate the forbidden zone near the Han River and save his daughter from the clutches of the horrifying Host.

title: Created Equal: The Premises and Promises of the Declaration of Independence
location: Regenstein Library, The Special Collections Research Center
description:
On July 2, 1776, the Continental Congress voted to declare independence from Great Britain. Two days later, delegates in Philadelphia finalized a document designed to announce and explain that act to readers in America and Europe.
 The Declaration of Independence asserted the revolutionary right of a people to alter or abolish a government, grounding that principle in the “self-evident” claims that “all Men are created Equal, that they are endowed by their Creator with certain unalienable Rights” and “that among these are Life, Liberty, and the Pursuit of Happiness.”
 Over time, many readers have come to consider the radical philosophical premises in the Declaration as founding political promises of the United States. In doing so, they transformed an indictment of the British King and a manifesto of secession from the British Empire into an American charter of liberty, equality, and rights.
 But the Declaration’s meaning has never been solitary. From the start, readers disagreed about what its authors intended. Since 1776, radically different interpretations of the Declaration’s ideas have been put to different ends—from demands for the legal, political, and social equality of all persons, to claims for the rights of states to secede from the union, to calls for the revolutionary overthrow of the government.
 How did the Declaration’s premises become its promises? Drawing on rare materials from the seventeenth century to the present, this exhibition invites you to explore the document’s meanings in its own time, to consider contested interpretations across history, and to reflect on what the Declaration means today.
 Curator
 Eric Slauter, Associate Professor, Department of English Language and Literature; Associate faculty member, Divinity School; Founding Director of the Karla Scherer Center for the Study of American Culture; The University of Chicago
 Visitors
 This exhibition is free and open to all. Visitors to the University of Chicago Library may obtain an entry pass by checking in at Regenstein Library’s entry desk and presenting a current, government-issued photo ID, such as a driver’s license, CityKey, state ID, or passport to confirm identity. Get more visitor information.
